"Your Majesty, it is time for morning court. Might this servant arrange for someone to come in and assist with Your Majesty's toilette?" The head eunuch's strangled, honeyed voice came through clearly.

"No court today. Have someone come in a little later." Su Wan called back, then turned and looked at Zhao Heng, now bundled up like a wrapped dumpling, and knitted her brows.

Just barely. Good thing she had watched enough palace dramas and made her preparations ahead of time.

And it wasn't her own blood.

"Your Majesty, the Minister of War insists that court must convene today." The eunuch kept his coaxing tone pleasant and accommodating. "Going a little later would be perfectly fine."

"Then I'll sleep a little longer." Su Wan affected the drowsy manner of someone not quite awake, and then made her move. She flipped Zhao Heng over, swung herself astride his back, and leaned down close to his ear, gritting out her warning. "Don't move. Don't make a sound. Or I'll send you to the Chamber of Ritual Affairs and let you learn for yourself what it means to lose your edge."

When did this man wake up, and how long had he been watching her?

Zhao Heng didn't stir.

Satisfied, Su Wan straightened up, worked loose the ropes binding him and tossed them aside, then rolled him over and got off. She took hold of his hands and hauled him up.

She couldn't let any cracks show. This was already the second time she had had this dream, and the plot had picked up right where it left off before she woke — she might well keep dreaming it in future.

What if she died in the dream one day, and died in real life along with it? She hadn't had her freedom yet.

Zhao Heng rose without much of an expression, eyes drooping as he looked down at her. In the dark depths of his pupils, her own solemn face was reflected back.

Su Wan, entirely unaware, reached for his waistband and pulled off the white outer robe, leaving him in the thin inner garment underneath.

She glanced at the firmly muscled chest beneath the fabric and slipped a hand inside.

In the next instant, Su Wan snatched her hand back as though she had touched a flame. Heat rose in her cheeks. She looked up at Zhao Heng with an entirely baffled expression.

"How dare you — you actually...! You actually...!"

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.content:
A night without dreams.

When he woke in the early morning, Qin Yuan was genuinely surprised.

He focused his thoughts and reflected carefully for a moment, confirming that he had truly not dreamed the night before.

Strange.

Of course, the precise reason remained unclear — but a night of undisturbed rest, free from the torment of strange dreams, was something to be grateful for. For him, it was a rare thing indeed.

His mood had been rather good these past few days.

Those close to him might not have noticed, but the inner-palace attendants at his side, and the seasoned officials who had served him for many years, could detect the subtle signs.

Minister Fang, for instance — a veteran of three reigns, with many years at court — had picked up on it with quiet acuity.

With the Emperor in good spirits, these subordinates of his felt the tightly wound string inside them ease, just slightly.

Minister Fang even found a spare moment to visit the family school and have a look around.

In the midst of a child's clear reading voice, Minister Fang found himself thinking of his second son, taken too young, and then of that beloved granddaughter of his with her exacting taste in beauty.

He sighed, and on an impulse, ordered one of his own chess manuals to be sent to Jiyao.

— He recalled that his late wife had mentioned it once, saying the second granddaughter had loved chess from a very young age.

That much, at least, she had inherited from him.

Jiyao was rather startled to suddenly receive a chess manual sent by her grandfather. "Grandfather gave this to me? Did he say anything when he sent it?"

"Only that the chess manual was to be given to the Second Young Miss. Nothing else was said."

Jiyao was even more puzzled. So Grandfather had personally sent her a chess manual, drenched in affection — just like that?

Whatever the elders chose to give, one had to be grateful.

Whatever Grandfather's reasons for sending it, Jiyao knew she ought to go and express her thanks in person. But when she went to find her grandfather, she was told that Minister Fang was occupied with official business and not at home, and that she should go back for now.

In the days that followed, Jiyao went several more times, and the situation was the same each time.

Jiyao had no choice but to let the matter rest for the time being.

All the same, after this series of visits, the low spirits that had settled over her on account of her father gradually began to lift back to normal.

That evening, Jiyao dreamed again.

In the dream, her father was an immortal in the heavens — a celestial horse with wings at his side, magnificent and otherworldly.

"Bao'er, come up and try." Her father dismounted and gave the horse a pat on its flank.

"How wonderful!" Jiyao's eyes lit up. "Then I'll give it a try."

She had never ridden a horse in real life, but in the dream her movements were clean and effortless — she swung herself up onto the horse's back in a single motion, took the reins in hand, and sat with her back perfectly straight.

The celestial horse first broke into a gallop across the ground, faster and faster, and then spread its wings and soared upward.

Jiyao gripped the reins with a light hand, letting herself drift freely among the clouds, feeling a joy too vast to put into words.

After a good while, she thought quietly to herself: stop. Go home.

Everything before her vanished in an instant, and Jiyao found herself back in the Begonia Courtyard, surrounded by peach trees in full bloom.

— Flying through the heavens was wonderful, but she seemed to love this dream "home" even more.

There was papa and mama here. And... her husband.

Right — her husband.

She hadn't been controlling her dreams these past few days and had nearly forgotten. She was a married woman in the dream. She wondered how her dream husband had been getting on.

With that thought, Jiyao walked briskly back to her room.

The moment she stepped inside, she saw the bridegroom who had not been long married into the household. He was sitting by the window reading, and rose slowly when he saw her come in, his brows composed and cool. "Where have you been?"

"I went riding with Papa." Jiyao stepped closer, took hold of his hand, and asked with a smile: "Were you thinking of me?"

……

The moment the girl came close, Qin Yuan became fully aware that he was having that strange dream again.

In recent nights he had been sleeping soundly, and had gone nearly half a month without dreaming. He had not expected the strange dream to come rolling back like a tide.

He gave a cold laugh inwardly, but quickly recomposed himself: this was, in fact, a perfect opportunity to practice the lucid dreaming method Priest Yun He had described.

If he could not shake free of the strange dream in the short term, he might as well become the master of it.

Whether in the waking world or in dreams, he could not be controlled by another.

Lucid dreaming, however, was no simple matter.

Qin Yuan quietly recalled the method Priest Yun He had described and tried to put it into practice. But at that very moment, his hand was already being held by the girl before him.

He heard himself reply: "Mm. I was."

"I knew it." Jiyao smiled, guided him back to sit down, then came around behind him and rested her chin affectionately on his shoulder. "I've been busy these past few days — you mustn't be cross with me."

The girl's soft form pressed lightly against his back. A faint fragrance drifted over.

"I'm not cross." As he said these words, Qin Yuan followed the lucid dreaming method and tried to hold his breath.

In the next instant, he truly could no longer smell the fragrance.

It was a small change, but it struck Qin Yuan like a thunderclap: it had actually worked. He had actually managed to hold his breath.

This was the first time he had ever done something within the strange dream that he himself had intended to do.

It seemed that as long as one grasped the method and started with the small details, given time, full control would inevitably follow.

Jiyao was entirely unaware of any of this.

She was accustomed to controlling dreams, but she did not plan out in advance every word and gesture of every person in the dream. As long as things moved in the right general direction, that was enough.

"What were you reading just now?" Jiyao leaned sideways and made idle conversation.

The bridegroom said nothing, and gestured for her to see for herself.

Jiyao leaned over, looked closely, and exclaimed in surprise: "A Treatise on Water Management?"

Goodness — was her inner mind really so preoccupied with matters of governance? A book she had only glimpsed once in Grandfather's study could appear in her dream as well?

"Yes." Qin Yuan replied, feeling inwardly rather wistful.

Looking at things as they currently stood, there was very little within the dream he could control, and the time available to him was not long. Otherwise, he could simply end the dream directly, or deal with the person inside it.

No hurry. Take it slowly.

He had never been short of patience.

Because this was a dream, Jiyao had no real interest in the specific contents of the Treatise on Water Management — she had no desire to look at a blank page.

She leaned half against the bridegroom, tapping idly at his palm with one finger, thoroughly bored.

Qin Yuan said nothing and let her do as she pleased. After several silent attempts, he finally managed to take hold of the girl's hand.

Another success.

Qin Yuan seized the opportunity and reached up to pull the girl away from his back.

He moved quickly. Qi Yao smiled faintly: Not a warm embrace? Could it be that you have other thoughts?

Well then, just hold her for a moment.

The thought had barely formed when Qin Yuan turned around and froze — the girl had already spun around on her own and fallen into his arms.

Soft and warm in his embrace, the murderous intent in Qin Yuan's heart rose again. — Yet once more, he lost control of the dream.

The girl was completely unaware. She stretched her arms around his waist, her cheek pressed and rubbing lightly against his chest.

The two were far too close at this moment.

From Qin Yuan's angle, he could see a small red birthmark behind her ear — like a single red plum blossom against pure white snow, strikingly vivid.

Gradually, the red plum grew blurrier and blurrier.

Qin Yuan woke from the dream.

He slowly opened his eyes, his gaze dim.

……

In the early morning, Qi Yao woke up and did not rise immediately.

She lay in bed for a while before sitting up, throwing off the covers.

Tomorrow was the wedding day of her cousin Zhao Jingyun, and the girls from the Fang family were coming today to perform the tianzhuang ceremony.

— The so-called tianzhuang ceremony was a custom of the time: on the day before a wedding, the bride's close friends and family would come to present gifts and offer their blessings.

The lady of the house learned of this and specially gave the Fang family cousins two days off.

After tidying up, Qi Yao and her four cousins rode together to the Zhao family home.

The wedding festivities were tomorrow, and the Zhao household was already decorated with lanterns and streamers, everything bright and new.

The bride-to-be Zhao Jingyun was in the inner chamber speaking with her mother when she heard that her maternal cousins had arrived. Overjoyed yet bashful, she quickly had them brought in, and laughed: "Why have you all come so early?"

"To add makeup for our cousin, of course — we wouldn't dare be late." The third young miss Fang Zhiru laughed and spoke, while the other Fang cousins presented the tianzhuang gifts they had prepared at the table.

The Fang family girls had discussed it beforehand — the gifts they brought were either gold and silver jewelry, or fine rouge and powder, or everyday necessities. None were worth a great fortune, but all were things the new bride would find useful in her daily life ahead.

Zhao Jingyun quickly had the servants take everything in, and pulled the cousins aside for a chat.

The young girls had not seen each other in a long time, and on top of that such a grand occasion had arisen — it seemed as though they had endless whispered things to say to each other.

But unfortunately, as the bride-to-be, the day before the wedding, Zhao Jingyun was exceptionally busy.

The Zhao family had no shortage of guests in the capital, and many had come to offer tianzhuang gifts for Zhao Jingyun. Besides the maternal cousins from her grandmother's family, there were also cousins from her paternal aunt's side, daughters of prominent families, and familiar neighbors' daughters.

Everyone had come bearing gifts and full of blessings. By rights, she ought to personally thank each one.

"You all go ahead and sit — wait a moment, I'll be right back." Zhao Jingyun settled her several cousins in the side hall, then hurried off to attend to things herself.

The remaining Fang family girls sipped tea and waited for their cousin to return.

They had barely drunk half a cup of tea when a commotion broke out outside.

Fang Mengyao was the youngest, only nine years old, and could never sit still. Hearing the noise, she tossed out a sentence — "I'll go take a look" — and ran off outside.

The eldest sister was pregnant and hadn't come today. Among this group of sisters, Qi Yao was the oldest, and could not help but look after the younger ones. Seeing the little one run off, Qi Yao felt uneasy and followed her out with a smile.

Land was precious in the capital, and the Zhao family's residence had only two courtyards. Children ran fast — in the blink of an eye, she had already run all the way into the main courtyard.

It was even livelier here.

It turned out the Zhao family was setting off firecrackers before the wedding, following the old custom of lighting bamboo to drive away evil and bad luck.

The bride's thirteen-year-old younger brother Zhao Jinde had also grabbed a few small firecrackers.

"Cousin brother, give me one, let me try." Fang Mengyao watched with eager, itching eyes.

Zhao Jinde was afraid of frightening her, so he only gave her a small toy called a "dripping gold." Then he glanced over and saw Qi Yao, and tossed one over to her as well: "Cousin sister, you play too."

Qi Yao took it, but had no intention of playing with it. She simply kept her eyes fixed on her younger cousin.

She wasn't trying to dampen her cousin's fun — she was genuinely worried.

Who would have thought that Fang Mengyao, in a moment of carelessness, would stuff an unlit "dripping gold" straight into Qi Yao's hand.

Seeing the sparks visibly spitting out, Qi Yao was startled and nearly threw it to the ground. But it would be too embarrassing in front of everyone, so she forced herself to endure it.

She raised it high, holding it as far from herself as possible.

Suddenly, Qi Yao heard a soft laugh. Then came a clear, composed voice: "What are you afraid of? This won't cause any trouble."

chapters.title: Chapter 7
chapters.content:
The voice was quite unfamiliar.

Qi Yao startled and turned to look — it was a young man of about eighteen or nineteen. He was tall and well-built, with an easy and refined air, currently gazing at the "dripping gold" in her hand with a faintly amused smile on his face.

She didn't recognize him and had no intention of engaging further. She simply gave a small nod, then turned back to urge her younger cousin toward the side hall: "Let's go back quickly, don't make your older sisters worry."

"Okay, okay." Fang Mengyao reluctantly pulled at her pouch, feeling secretly deflated.

She knew her second older sister was timid, but she hadn't expected that even a five-year-old's "dripping gold" could frighten her.

Still, out of consideration for her second sister's pride, Fang Mengyao refrained from teasing her further, and obediently let her sister take her by the hand back to the side hall.

As the two sisters were leaving, they faintly heard from behind them Zhao Jinde's excited voice: "Cousin brother, you came too!"

"Of course — such a big occasion, how could I not come?" It was that same clear, composed voice.

Qi Yao's heart stirred slightly. The Zhao family cousin referred to this person as "cousin brother," yet she didn't recognize him — so he must be a relative on the paternal side of her father's family.

She had heard her elder sister mention it before: the Zhao family had three paternal aunts, all living in the capital. He was probably from one of those households.

Naturally, this had nothing to do with her.

The two sisters quickly returned to the side hall. The Zhao family cousin had still not come back yet.

The girls waited in the side hall for quite a while before Zhao Jingyun finally hurried in, her face full of apologetic smiles: "I'm so sorry, I've kept you all waiting."

"It's nothing, we haven't been here long." Everyone knew how busy she was — how could anyone complain?

Zhao Jingyun had no sisters of her own, and she got along extremely well with her maternal cousins. She brought them into her bedroom and generously showed them the wedding dress, cape, and pearl-embroidered shoes she would wear that day, as well as the hairstyle she planned for tomorrow and the rouge and powder she would use.

Everyone exclaimed in admiration.

Zhao Jingyun then shared her joy and nervousness with her cousins.

A girl who was usually so bright and composed — faced with such a momentous occasion, she could not help feeling anxious.

Qi Yao was a woman of few words, but she was calm and composed by nature, and was well-suited to listening. As for words of comfort, those were left to the cousins to provide.

Before they knew it, dusk had fallen. Zhao Jingyun couldn't bear to let her cousins leave, and suggested they all stay the night.

"That might be difficult......" Qi Yao's expression grew slightly awkward. If it were just herself it would be fine, but she had brought four cousins with her this time, the youngest only nine years old — who could let her sleep outside?

"Then alright, you must all come early tomorrow." Zhao Jingyun understood her concern and pressed no further.

Qi Yao agreed, giving a small nod.

Just then, a maternal aunt who hadn't been seen for a long time also hurried over, and persuaded them warmly: "You children really are something. This is your aunt's home, not some stranger's place. Why bother going back? Besides, I've already had the guest rooms prepared."

As she waved her hand to gesture, a thin booklet slipped out from her sleeve and fell down.

With a light thud, it landed, by coincidence, right in front of Qi Yao.

Qi Yao saw this and without thinking much, bent down to pick it up.

Unexpectedly, the aunt's expression changed in an instant — quick as lightning and before she could cover it, she snatched the booklet away with one swift grab.

Qi Yao was caught completely off guard. In that brief moment, she caught only a glimpse of five characters on the cover of the booklet: 《枕间风月图》— "Pillow Boudoir Pictures." In the blink of an eye, the booklet was stuffed back into the aunt's sleeve.

"I......" Qi Yao blinked in confusion, and hastily explained, "Auntie, I was only helping to pick it up."

Truly, with all her heart, she had had absolutely no intention of peeking at that booklet.

The aunt smiled somewhat awkwardly: "I know, good girl. Auntie didn't mean anything by it. It's just that this booklet is for the new bride — it's meant to be placed in her dowry chest. Not suitable for an unmarried young girl to see."

Tomorrow her daughter was to be married, and she had privately wanted to teach her a few things about the marriage bed — so she had hidden this illustrated book in her sleeve, planning to slip it to her daughter when no one was around. She hadn't expected it to fall out right in front of everyone.

Alas, she should have kept it tucked closer to her chest.

And this girl from the Fang family was also truly unlucky — she really shouldn't have seen any of it.

"Oh." Qi Yao was naturally adept at reading situations and keeping the peace. Hearing her aunt say this, she asked no further. She bid farewell to her aunt and cousin, and headed home together with her several cousins.

Sitting in the carriage on the way back, Fang Mengyao asked curiously: "Second sister, what kind of book was that? Why did Auntie get so flustered over it?"

"I don't know either." Feeling somewhat embarrassed, Qi Yao waved her hand dismissively, not bringing up the book's title, and only said: "I didn't get a clear look just now."

Beside her, Zhi Yao lifted her chin: "I know a little."

"What is it? Third sister, tell us."

"It seems to be some kind of illustrated book. When eldest sister came back three days after her wedding, I happened to overhear a few words. Little Mengyao, don't be in such a rush — wait until you're married yourself, then you'll know."

Fang Mengyao was nine years old. Hearing the word "married," she felt both anxious and embarrassed, and turned her head to look at Qi Yao, the oldest among them: "Second sister, look at third sister — she's teasing me again."

"Who's teasing anyone? You were the one who asked first." Zhi Yao deliberately made a face at her younger sister.

"You two stop it." Qi Yao rarely took on the role of mediating between others, and wasn't particularly good at it either. She somewhat forcibly changed the subject: "What time are we setting off tomorrow?"

Zhi Yao thought about it: "We're going to see the bride off, so naturally the earlier the better."

"Mm." Fang Mengyao nodded in agreement.

With the topic shifted, everyone settled down, and Qi Yao quietly let out a small breath of relief.

For some reason, she suddenly thought again of the illustrated booklet that had slipped from her aunt's sleeve.

At the time she had only glanced at it without a second thought, and hadn't taken in the specific contents of the booklet — but based on her aunt's flustered reaction and her cousins' guesses, Qi Yao vaguely understood it had something to do with matters of the inner chambers.

She couldn't help feeling a little curious.

And besides — the cover of that booklet looked somewhat familiar. As though she had seen it somewhere before.

Where had it been?

Qi Yao couldn't recall for the moment, and didn't dwell on it further.

The group returned home. It was already quite late. Qi Yao spent some time on her evening routine, washed up, and went to bed early.

Half-asleep and drowsy — just as she was about to drift off — Qi Yao's mind suddenly stirred, and her eyes snapped open.

She remembered.

That copy of "Pillow Boudoir Pictures" — she had indeed seen it before. It had been in her father's study.

Back then her father was still alive, and she had been only five or six, not knowing many characters yet. One day, she had sneaked into her father's study to play and wanted to flip through some of the illustrated books. She had casually picked one up, but before she could even open it, her father discovered her.

"Little one, this isn't for you to look at." Her father had taken the illustrated book and hidden it high up in a cabinet behind a thick volume, then found another picture book to give her instead.

So many years had passed that she had nearly forgotten all about it. But today, that booklet's beautiful cover and the three characters "风月图"¹ had stirred up her old memories.

Thinking of old times, Qi Yao's drowsiness faded considerably.

She let out a sigh, and after a while drifted off to sleep again.

Perhaps it was thinking of her childhood that did it. That night, Qi Yao dreamed of herself as a little girl.

Her parents had both been young then — her father would half-cradle her in his arms and teach her to recognize characters.

Her mother sat nearby doing needlework, saying that the Duanyang Festival was coming soon, and that she would make her five-poison pouches to ward off evil and keep her healthy as she grew up.

Qi Yao knew she was dreaming. But the scene was too warm and tender, and she had no wish to force herself awake — she was content to stay in the dream as her child-self, together with her parents.

A night of sweet dreams.

The next day, Qi Yao rose early. After tidying up properly, she and her cousins set off once again for the Zhao family home.

Today was the day of her cousin's wedding. The third sister-in-law and fourth sister-in-law also went along with the sisters.

With elders present, Qi Yao felt more at ease. She quietly tucked herself to one side and watched peacefully as her cousin was surrounded by people helping with her makeup, changing her clothes, offering prayers, accepting greetings, and weeping with joy.

She had previously witnessed her cousin-sister being married off, and now watching her cousin again — the process was much the same — yet Qi Yao still couldn't help reddening her eyes several times.

Amid a burst of firecrackers, the new bride was carried up onto the bridal sedan.

The procession of well-wishers departed, and the Zhao family fell quiet again.

The aunt wept without stopping.

— It was the custom in the capital that on the day of the wedding, the bride's uncles and brothers would follow the procession and escort the new bride to her husband's home. The bride's own parents, however, could not go along.

Several women offered comfort in turn: "What is there to cry about? A happy occasion — one shouldn't cry. Your daughter has good character and won't be marrying far away. Whenever you miss her, you can see her anytime."

"I know." The aunt wiped her eyes while saying, "I made you all laugh — I truly hadn't meant to cry."

She understood it all in her mind. She simply couldn't help herself.

What Qi Yao could not say aloud, she silently passed a handkerchief over and refilled her aunt's tea.

A thought drifted through her mind: if grandfather and grandmother were still alive, they certainly would not have been willing to let her marry away.

That brought Fang Shen's tears to a halt at last.

By the time they left it was not early, and Fang's third madam and fourth madam took the younger ones home together.

The group returned home; it was already dark. The girls still had to attend their women's studies lessons the next day.

But Qi Yao was not yet sleepy. She rested for a little while, and not wanting anyone to accompany her, quietly carried a small lamp by herself and pushed open the door to her father's study.

Her father had been gone for nearly ten years, yet this study had always been kept exactly as it was — every so often, someone would come specifically to clean it.

Following her memory, Qi Yao walked to the bookcase and held up the lamp. Sure enough, she found that thick volume on the upper shelf of the cabinet.

Catching sight of it, Qi Yao's heart gave a small leap.

It seemed her memory had not been wrong after all. She just didn't know what was actually inside it.

Qi Yao steadied herself, reached up, and took down the thick book.

The thick book was hollow inside — a thin booklet had been hidden within it.

In the lamplight she could see clearly: it was the "Pillow Boudoir Pictures." On the cover were also a few small characters: Essential for the inner chambers. Illustrations exquisitely crafted.

Brimming with curiosity, Qi Yao opened the booklet.

After just one glance, her face flushed crimson.

(TL: those three characters 风月图 just means wind, moon painting. I was conflicted on whether to translate it, but decided to leave it as is, since the authors said 'characters')

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.content:
The illustrations in the booklet depicted a naked man and woman, entangled together just like that.

Qi Yao felt her face flush with a "whoosh," heat rolling in like waves, burning from her cheeks all the way down to her neck — scorching terribly. How could she look more carefully? Even worse would be if someone caught her looking at something like this.

Without another thought, she flung the booklet in her hand far away, and at the same time shut her eyes tightly, her heart pounding wildly.

After a moment, Qi Yao came back to her senses and realized — there was no one else here, and no one would come to see.

Thinking this, her courage grew considerably.

She hesitated for a little while, then bent down to retrieve the booklet again. It was still a bit embarrassing, though. So she took a deep breath, shut one eye, and peeked at it with the other.

To speak plainly — the paper quality of this booklet was excellent, showing no deterioration after so many years. The illustrations were exquisite, every fine detail rendered without the slightest omission. But the content of the pictures was truly far too bold, far too uninhibited.

And there were small characters beside them too — something about "extreme pleasure," something about "soul-melting"......

Qi Yao had never seen any of this before, and had never even thought about it.

She had originally assumed that two people holding hands, embracing, kissing — that was already the most intimate thing between a man and woman. She had never imagined there could be this — flesh joined to flesh, bodies intertwined.

Heavens!

Qi Yao's face burned scorching hot, and a wave of indescribable numbness and tingling surged through her chest, her body inexplicably growing somewhat warm.

She was perfectly clear in her mind that this booklet was not something an unmarried young lady should be reading. If others found out, she would have no face left. But curiosity drove her on, and she turned to the next page.

After taking in the contents of the next illustration, Qi Yao's eyes went wide once more.

Between people — things could actually be like this?!

Qi Yao was dumbfounded, and continued turning the pages, growing more astonished with every one.

Such a thin little booklet, and yet it contained so many different ways!

After a long while, Qi Yao finally hid the booklet back inside the thick volume and carefully put it back in its original place.

After leaving the study, she stood in the courtyard for quite some time.

The cool night breeze brushed against her, chilling her flushed cheeks. Once her face was no longer so hot, Qi Yao returned to her room and sat down at the table.

"Miss, miss......" The voice of Shuangxi suddenly rang out in her ear.

Qi Yao forced herself back to her senses: "Mm? What is it?"

Shuangxi's eyes were full of puzzlement: "Wasn't miss going to the second master's study to look for a book? Didn't you find it?"

She had seen her miss come back empty-handed, and so she asked this.

"Oh, right, I didn't find it — it's too dark, there are too many books, I'll look again tomorrow." Qi Yao replied in a muddled rush, then picked up the already-cold teacup and drained it in one go.

Shuangxi was startled, nearly moving to stop her, and frowned: "The tea is cold, miss — why are you still drinking it? Let me pour you some hot."

Qi Yao only smiled, and did not ask for more hot tea.

She absentmindedly washed up, changed into her sleeping clothes, and lay quietly on the bed.

Qi Yao had always slept well, but tonight she tossed and turned, unable to drift off.

Every time she closed her eyes, the images from that booklet flooded her mind.

She tried to chase them away, but they wouldn't leave.

At one moment the figures in the illustrations were themselves, and then in the next instant they had taken on someone else's face.

It was not until nearly the fourth watch of the night that Qi Yao finally drifted off in a daze.

Having slept poorly the night before, Qi Yao was inevitably somewhat distracted the next day at women's studies.

The lady of the house assumed she was feeling sentimental over her cousin's marriage, and didn't scold her much — instead she told her to go and rest properly.

Qi Yao felt both guilty and relieved, and quickly rose to take her leave.

She forcibly suppressed those tangled and chaotic thoughts, focused her mind and concentrated on her studies. It was not until bedtime that the associations began to surface again.

Could that be what they called the legendary "a single spring night worth a thousand gold"? Was it the bridal chamber candlelight? Was it the intimacy of husband and wife? Was it the ultimate pleasure spoken of between people?

She had no idea what it actually felt like.

Why not — try it in a dream? In dreams she had become intimate with someone, and there was even a gentleman there. It had no effect on reality whatsoever.

Having made up her mind, Qi Yao closed her eyes and drifted peacefully to sleep.

Before long, she entered the realm of dreams once more.

In the dream, her mother quietly handed her a booklet, looking mysterious: "Little one, when you get married, your mother will be busy. There is something I forgot to give you."

"What is it?" Qi Yao asked knowingly.

"You'll know when you go back to your room — remember to look at it together with your husband." Her mother whispered softly.

Qi Yao gave a nod, took the booklet, and headed back to the room.

In the dream it was already dark. The room was lit with two candles, and the entire inner chamber was veiled in a layer of warm amber light.

The gentleman was reading. He had apparently just bathed, dressed in a plain and clean sleeping robe, his hair slightly damp at the temples. His collar was loosely open, revealing a small patch of skin at his chest.

Qi Yao's face grew inexplicably warm. She steadied herself, greeted him as naturally as she could: "Husband, I'm back."

"Why were you gone so long?"

"Mother just sent for me." Qi Yao stepped closer, moving to his side. Thinking of what she was about to do, she felt herself tense up involuntarily by a few degrees.

......

Qin Yuan knew he was dreaming.

This was the sixth time he had had this strange dream, and he was already considerably calmer than before. His rage and murderous intent had been temporarily suppressed, and there was only one thought in his mind: this time, he must take control of this dream.

As the woman drew near, Qin Yuan employed the method the Taoist priest of Yunhe had spoken of, and silently attempted it — successfully stroking her collar.

Good. Though barely perceptible, it was still progress.

Qi Yao had not noticed these small details.

She took the gentleman's hand, her face flushed as she said softly: "Come, let us look at something together."

"Dream control" failed again at this moment. Qin Yuan said nothing, and let her lead him by the hand, the two of them sitting side by side on the edge of the bed.

Qi Yao placed the booklet on her knees, and with great seriousness turned to the first page.

Qin Yuan glanced sideways — and his heart gave a sudden lurch.

No — what on earth is this? She was actually showing him this?!

Qin Yuan naturally knew of such illustrated books, and had even glimpsed with his own eyes the intimate scenes between men and women in his younger years.

But what did it mean for this woman in the dream to be showing him this? The previous times she had always stopped at the critical moment — was she intending to go all the way this time?

He wanted to immediately fling her hand away and toss this booklet far off. Then block this young woman's path and warn her never to appear in his dreams again.

But at this very moment, his just-practiced "dream control" failed him, and he could only stare fixedly at the illustration before his eyes.

The two figures in the picture were intertwined in a strangely contorted position, with small annotated characters printed neatly beside it.

Feeling she had looked at enough, Qi Yao reached out to cover the illustrated book, then turned to look at the gentleman. Her gaze was soft and hazy, as though carrying sparks of fire, her voice gentle enough to make one's bones go weak, yet with a barely concealed eagerness: "Husband, shall we try?"

Qin Yuan's gaze fell on her face beyond his control.

He still could not remember her features, but at this moment he could see her bright and glistening eyes, her reddened lips, and the distinct flush across her cheeks. As though there were an invisible thread binding him, compelling him — without his knowing — to draw closer and closer to her.

Qi Yao tilted her head up to kiss him.

The two had kissed before in the dream, but this time was clearly different.

Qi Yao had looked at the illustrated book and knew there was more to kissing than simply pressing lips together. She gathered her courage and lightly parted hers.

The soft touch of lips transmitted itself to him, and Qin Yuan wanted to push her away — but he had completely lost control of himself. Not only did he respond fervently to the kiss, he even traced the tip of his tongue along her lips.

This was undeniably a probing and suggestive gesture.

Qi Yao's body went light, her heart fluttered faintly, a hidden tension building inside her, and an indescribable, difficult-to-articulate anticipation.

This was likely the most genuine voice deep within her. The gentleman cupped her face in one hand for a deep kiss, the other hand moving to undo her clothing.

At this very moment, Qin Yuan suddenly discovered he could act freely again.

Good — his dream control had recovered just in time.

He abruptly ended the kiss, only to find that between the two of them a faint silvery thread had stretched out — his expression darkened involuntarily.

"Husband, what's wrong?" Qi Yao was somewhat surprised, her pair of eyes misty and hazy, like a fine mist veiling clouds, her reddened lips still bearing the traces of the kiss just moments ago.

Qin Yuan said nothing, his expression growing even more forbidding.

It had only been a kiss, and yet his body had already produced an obvious reaction.

The young woman's clothing was half-slipped from her shoulders, revealing white and rounded skin, her head turned slightly sideways as she looked at him, her eyes confused and bewildered, not quite understanding.

Qi Yao truly did not understand — hadn't she already made up her mind to try it in the dream?

Could it be that she still harbored other thoughts deep down? Or was it that she was actually far too timid at heart?

It shouldn't be.

Suddenly, out of the corner of her eye, she noticed the conspicuous anomaly beneath the gentleman's sleeping robe — and with curiosity, she reached out and lightly touched it.

Qin Yuan's body stiffened in an instant, reflexively grabbing her hand, his other hand meanwhile reaching out toward her slender and delicate neck.

Then, in that split second, he once again lost control of his body in the dream.

The hand that had touched her skin — its original grip had turned into a gentle caress.

He slowly drew closer, letting the young woman wrap her arms around his waist.

The moment that soft and warm body pressed against him, Qin Yuan felt only his scalp go numb. The murderous intent mingled with the desire surging within him, growing more and more rampant.

For a moment it was hard to tell which was heavier.

Finally, he leaned his whole body over her.

Exactly like the illustration.

chapters.title: Chapter 9
chapters.content:
Qi Yao didn't know how to describe this feeling.

It was as though a warm current flowed softly through her body, a tingling numbness spreading to all four limbs and a hundred bones. She gripped the gentleman's shoulders and wanted to say something — but her mind was a blank, and she could only call out his name softly in a faint voice.

The sound was so coquettish that even she herself flushed red to the ears upon hearing it.

The gentleman showed no signs of stopping, seemingly without knowledge of fatigue.

Then suddenly, his movements ceased.

Qi Yao was somewhat dazed, and blinked in confusion.

Strange — why? This wasn't what she had intended at all.

Qin Yuan could no longer hold back a sneer. After so long, he had finally managed to regain control. He pried away the woman's hand that was draped over his shoulder, intending to bring this absurd scene before him to a direct end.

Yet the woman beneath him was completely unguarded, and even reached up to help wipe a bead of sweat from his brow.

This one small gesture brought the two of them even closer together.

Qin Yuan went rigid, his scalp prickling, nearly letting out a groan. In that instant he once again lost control of his body.

In the dream, every sensation felt abnormally real — the creak and sway of the bed, the faint swaying of the bed curtains, the fragrance from the woman's body, and that soul-melting sweetness......

He clearly resisted all of this, yet inexplicably he was also somewhat entranced.

Suddenly, a flash of white light seemed to streak across his mind.

Qin Yuan's heart gave a jolt.

The dream came to an abrupt end......

The night sky was deep and dark.

Qin Yuan knew he had broken free from the dream.

As though having just lived through a fierce and grueling battle, his chest heaved, he could not sleep, and he slowly exhaled a long breath.

He was awake.

Recalling the scenes in the dream, Qin Yuan's heart was filled with fury.

He was the Emperor, holding all authority in the real world — yet in dreams he had fallen to such a state, being manipulated and toyed with by a woman of unknown origin.

This was truly the greatest shame and humiliation.

Qin Yuan did not rush to rise, but instead shut his eyes tightly and let his thoughts race rapidly. — In the dream control method spoken of by the Taoist priest of Yunhe, what one did after waking was also of great importance.

He could not go on like this. He must gain complete mastery of the dream.

After roughly the time it takes for an incense stick to burn, Qin Yuan finally rose, calmly ordered the inner attendants to bring water, and dealt with the traces left on his body.

......

The Ministry of Rites.

Qi Yao woke with a start, not wishing to dwell on the feeling of the dream, and hastily threw back the bed covers.

— Only then did she feel a dull ache in her lower back, and a faint soreness in her lower abdomen, as though her monthly flow had come.

Sure enough — her guess had been right.

It being the middle of the night, Qi Yao did not wish to call anyone. She lit the lamp by the bed herself and rummaged for her sanitary cloth.

She had tried to move quietly, but still startled Shuangxi who was sleeping in the outer room.

"Miss, why are you up?" Shuangxi came in holding a lamp, dressed in her outer clothes: "Do you need water?"

"No, looking for my sanitary cloth." Qi Yao replied in a muddled voice.

Shuangxi understood immediately, and hurried to lower the lamp: "Miss lie back down, I'll find it."

Qi Yao's everyday clothing was all collected by Shuangxi. She quickly found the replacement garments, helped her get sorted, and poured her a bowl of brown sugar water.

"It's still early — miss sleep a little longer." Shuangxi carried the lamp back to the outer room.

Qi Yao gave a soft sound of acknowledgment, blew out the lamp, and lay back down.

The brown sugar water warmed her pleasantly, and the slight discomfort in her body was almost ignorable. Qi Yao closed her eyes, and scenes from the dream involuntarily floated up in her mind.

She slowly pressed her hands against her flushing cheeks.

Too stimulating. Far too stimulating.

Even now thinking back on it, her mouth was dry and her heart pounded wildly.

Qi Yao shut her eyes and did her best to calm herself. After quite a long while, she finally managed to fall back asleep.

This time she had no more dreams, and when she opened her eyes it was already daylight.

As usual, after breakfast Qi Yao went off to women's studies.

It was another ordinary and fulfilling day.

These few days, as her body was not at its best, Qi Yao made no deliberate effort to dream, and naturally did not meet the gentleman in the dream either.

In the evening, Qi Yao finished her studies.

Just as she returned to Haiyuan Courtyard, Shuangxi came forward to greet her: "Miss, there is something curious to tell you."

"What is it?"

"Someone came today to propose a match for the third young miss."

Qi Yao was mildly surprised: "Third sister? Hasn't third sister already been betrothed?"

"That's right, so the third master rejected them outright."

Qi Yao gave a small nod and thought nothing more of it. A family coming to seek a girl — perfectly normal. That household had probably come to the door on a whim without first inquiring properly.

Who would have known that the very next day this matter would actually come around to her.

Again it was Shuangxi who told her. Shuangxi was a girl born and raised in the household — the maidservants and younger sisters-in-law were all in other courtyards, and news reached her with remarkable swiftness.

"Miss, the Wen family has come again today."

Qi Yao didn't understand: "What Wen family?"

"The very family that came yesterday to propose a match for the third young miss. Today their young master came in person — he says the one he wants to marry is the second young miss, not the third."

Qi Yao grew more and more astonished: "Me? How could it be me......"

Just then, a somewhat unfamiliar coarse-looking young manservant stepped forward and said: "Second young miss, the old master asks you to come to his study."

"Right now?"

"Yes, the old master is waiting."

Grandfather wished to see her. Qi Yao didn't bother with further tidying, and hurried over at once.

From a distance she could already see that the study had its lights on.

A thought flashed briefly through Qi Yao's mind: grandfather had been acting somewhat different lately each time she came to see him.

Entering through the door, she saw only her grandfather standing with his hands clasped behind his back, gazing at a landscape painting on the wall.

"Granddaughter pays her respects to grandfather." Qi Yao stepped forward and gave a proper bow.

Scholar Fang turned around: "You've heard as well?"

Qi Yao wasn't sure which matter her grandfather was referring to: "Heard what?"

"A few days ago, when your cousin from the Zhao family was being married off and you went to the Zhao home — did you happen to see anyone there?"

"There were quite a few people at the Zhao family those two days, I don't know which one grandfather is referring to." Qi Yao's heart gave a small leap and she grew somewhat tense.

Those two days she had spent most of the time accompanying her cousin and aunt, and had indeed seen a few unfamiliar faces, but had had no interaction with any of them.

Scholar Fang let out a sigh: "Wen Jiulang is the new neighbor from the same lane. He helped with the welcoming procession that day and said he caught a glimpse of you at the welcome ceremony and was immediately taken with you......"

Hearing the words "new neighbor from the same lane" and "welcome ceremony," Qi Yao blinked, and tried hard to search her memory. But at the time her attention had been entirely on her cousin — she had not the slightest impression of anyone nearby.

"......That Wen Jiulang's parents came to propose the match. His father couldn't hold back and agreed on his behalf, but it was the Wen family husband and wife who came to the door yesterday, openly seeking your third younger sister in marriage — and they were turned down by your third uncle. Today Wen Jiulang came himself, saying his parents had gotten it wrong, and that the one his heart truly wishes to marry is you......"

Scholar Fang finished speaking and shifted his gaze to his granddaughter, seeing her expression somewhat dazed, not knowing what she was thinking.

He thought of something and raised his eyebrows slightly: "You wouldn't actually think it was his parents who got it wrong, would you?"

"No." Qi Yao replied without thinking.

She was not that naive — how could a matter of marriage be mentioned without first making things clear? Besides, even if they had gotten it wrong at the start, he should have come to clarify it with his parents, not show up here himself.

— After all, it was his parents who came to the door first.

"That Wen Jiulang's character is not bad, and he has some ability. Today he came with clear eyes and an open heart, which shows he is not muddleheaded. Whether it was his parents who were displeased with you and deliberately came seeking your third sister, or whether he himself came to try his luck — the Wen family is not a good match." Scholar Fang said in a steady voice.

Qi Yao felt he was right, and quickly said: "Grandfather is correct."

"So I refused them." Scholar Fang's gaze came to rest on his granddaughter, and he continued: "I had you called here to tell you clearly in person — I didn't want this to cause any rift between you and your third sister."

Scholar Fang ran a strict household and was least fond of muddled and messy affairs.

"Grandfather need not worry — I am not one of those muddleheaded people, how could I fall out with third sister over something like this?"

Scholar Fang nodded with satisfaction, and his tone softened a few degrees involuntarily: "It's good that you can think this way."

It seemed this child, though usually quiet and unassuming, still had a clear head. She had not been led astray by Wen Jiulang's pursuit and grown confused.

"Have you been looking at the chess manual I had sent to you the other day?" Scholar Fang asked again.

"Yes, I look at it every day."

"Mm." Scholar Fang gave a small nod. "If there is anything you don't understand, come and ask."

"Yes."

Scholar Fang was not ordinarily a man of many words, yet somehow he seemed to have no shortage of things to say to this particular granddaughter.

Once the proper matters were concluded, the two quickly fell into a comfortable silence.

With a light cough, Scholar Fang once again took a chess manual from the bookcase and handed it to Qi Yao: "This manual is quite good — it's one I acquired in my early years. Take it home and have a look."

"Many thanks, grandfather." Qi Yao accepted it respectfully.

"It's getting late, you go back first."

"Yes." Qi Yao gave a proper bow, took the chess manual, and withdrew.

As evening gradually fell, Ji Yao walked along the road back to Haitang Courtyard, holding the chess manual in her hand, feeling alternately a sharp pang of sadness and a warm glow in her heart.

Normally, she did not often see her grandfather, yet she could say she had always lived under his protection. All her daily needs were provided by him. Even matters of marriage, which were traditionally decided by elders, he respected her opinion.

He even took the trouble to explain the reasons when she refused a marriage proposal.

Her grandfather was truly good to her.

Once she returned to Haitang Courtyard, Shuangxi immediately hurried forward, her face full of concern and worry. “Miss, how are you?”

Ji Yao knew what she was asking and did not hide anything, briefly recounting what had just happened.

“You refused…?” Shuangxi pressed her lips together, a trace of regret in her expression.

The Third Miss was already engaged. It was rare for someone to come to propose to the Second Miss, and yet it had turned into such an awkward situation.

However, Ji Li’s reaction was calm, giving only a light, “Mm.” In her view, her grandfather’s standards were not high; she did not feel regret for someone even he did not favor.

Moreover, she now had a Langjun in her dreams, having just experienced pleasure with him. She was in no hurry to marry.

Thinking of the Langjun from her dream, Ji Yao’s thoughts stirred slightly.

Come to think of it, she had not seen him for several nights.

She actually missed him a little.

chapters.title: The Accident
chapters.content:
Grandfather's birthday was coming up soon.

Grand Secretary Fang was known for his clean and upright conduct in office. This year was not a milestone age, so he certainly would not make a grand affair of it. But as his granddaughter, Jiyao wanted to prepare a heartfelt gift.

The trouble was, no matter how long she thought about it, nothing came to her. As the date drew steadily closer, she finally settled on painting a Longevity Offering scroll.

It was a conventional choice, perhaps, but it was her sincerest expression of love and reverence for her grandfather.

Grand Secretary Fang had placed third in the imperial examinations as a young man. The family carried a deep culture of learning, and regardless of whether a child was a son or a daughter, once they reached a certain age, they were sent to school.

Jiyao had attended the girls' academy, where she received a basic education in music, chess, calligraphy, and painting. Chess was her greatest love, but perhaps because her father was gifted in brushwork, she had inherited a measure of talent for painting as well.

Once her mind was made up, Jiyao used whatever spare moments she had to work on the piece.

She revised and repainted the Longevity Offering scroll, stopping and starting again, until the third attempt finally satisfied her — though just barely.

"The young miss has painted it so beautifully," Shuangxi said, standing behind her. "Shall we send it out to be mounted?"

Jiyao shook her head. "I'll take it myself when the rest day comes."

For one thing, the mounting of a gift required certain instructions she would have to give in person. For another, she welcomed any excuse to step outside.

After all, going out in a dream and going out in the real world were not quite the same thing.

The girls' academy ran on a relaxed schedule, with one rest day every five days.

When the day came, Jiyao notified her Third Aunt, who oversaw the household's domestic affairs, and left the manor with Shuangxi.

The capital was full of mounting shops, each with its own style and character.

Jiyao was not certain of her grandfather's exact preferences, but she had read through her father's personal notes and knew he favored the Suzhou style of mounting. She reasoned her grandfather likely felt the same. So she deliberately sought out a Suzhou-style shop.

The moment she stepped inside, she was greeted by several mounted paintings hanging along the walls. The style was delicate and understated, precisely what she had in mind.

The craftsman examined the painting she had brought and asked, in the usual manner: "How would you like it mounted? A hanging scroll? A hand scroll? An album?"

"A hanging scroll."

"Do you have preferences for the color or pattern of the silk border?"

Jiyao considered. "Light yellow for the mounting silk, and use an auspicious cloud pattern."

"Very good." The craftsman nodded, his brush flying across a small ledger as he jotted everything down. "That will be two taels of silver in total. Come back in five days to collect it. We ask for one tael as a deposit upfront."

Jiyao gave a small nod, and Shuangxi promptly produced a tael of loose silver.

With the arrangements settled, Jiyao and Shuangxi collected their receipt slip and stepped back out onto the street.

It was still early. Rather than heading straight home, Jiyao made a detour to a nearby bookshop.

Inside, a few customers were browsing in quiet contemplation, and the shop boy lounged lazily against the counter.

The moment Jiyao walked in, someone let out a startled cry: "Miss Fang!"

A young man strode quickly toward her, unable to hide the delight in his voice. "It really is you!"

Jiyao paused, studying him. He looked to be around seventeen or eighteen, fair-skinned and bright-eyed, dressed in the loose scholar's robe that was fashionable among young men of learning. She turned the face over carefully in her mind and was certain she did not recognize him. "You are...?" she asked, hesitantly.

"My surname is Wen. I am the ninth in my family..."

Jiyao's eyelid twitched. She understood at once who he was.

Shuangxi caught on as well and gave her mistress a discreet pinch on the arm. "Miss, it's that..."

The bookshop was quiet. The other patrons had all turned to look.

Jiyao had always been reserved and unassuming, and she detested being the center of attention. A flutter of anxiety rose in her chest. She managed a stiff nod, then grabbed Shuangxi's hand and started toward the door.

But the young man, Wen the Ninth, hurried after her. "Miss Fang, we have met before. On the eighth day of the first month, at the Zhao family's wedding. I am a classmate of Congzhou's."

The "Congzhou" he mentioned was Ye Congzhou, Zhao Jinyun's new husband.

The street outside was busy with passersby, and he kept pace behind her without letting up. Not wanting to cause a scene, Jiyao reluctantly stopped. "I know who you are. But I am on my way home now."

Wen the Ninth spoke quickly: "Miss Fang, I only want to explain. I never meant to slight you. It was only that back then..."

On the eighth day of the fourth month, he had seen the second miss of the Fang family at Ye Congzhou's wedding reception. The hall had been full of guests, and she had stood quietly beside Madam Zhao, composed and still.

Her complexion shone like luminous jade, her beauty without equal in the room.

Wen the Ninth felt his heart skip a beat.

When he returned home that evening, he could not settle. He made discreet inquiries and learned who she was, then begged his parents to approach the Fang family with a marriage proposal. His parents refused at first. Only after he pleaded at length did they reluctantly agree.

But what Wen the Ninth never anticipated was that his own parents had deceived him.

They had promised to seek the hand of the second miss of the Fang family. Yet when they arrived at the Fang household, the proposal somehow became one for the third miss instead. By the time Wen the Ninth learned of this, it was already too late. He had gone to the Fang family the following day to explain himself, but it had done nothing to change the outcome.

A son does not speak ill of his father's conduct. Standing before the second miss herself, Wen the Ninth could not reveal the truth in full. He said only, vaguely: "My father misheard, and a misunderstanding arose from it. But my intentions toward you were sincere. When I first saw you, I—"

"Mind your words," Jiyao cut him off sharply, her voice low and urgent. "There is no need to say any of this to me. Whatever needed to be said, the elders of my family have already made clear."

Had he lost his mind? In broad daylight, on a public street, saying things like "sincere intentions" and "love at first sight"...

Jiyao tugged Shuangxi's sleeve and walked away at a brisk pace.

The family's carriage was parked some distance away, and they still had a stretch to walk before reaching it.

Watching her go, Wen the Ninth panicked. He rushed ahead and planted himself in their path. "Miss Fang!"

He had, truth be told, been making his peace with reality. But this chance encounter today felt like a gift from heaven, and in an instant, his foolish hope reignited. He was determined to try once more.

Blocked so suddenly, Jiyao's face went pale. She veered to the side — and was blocked again.

She was just about to speak when a hand shot out from the side and gripped Wen the Ninth firmly by the shoulder.

A voice followed, one she found faintly familiar: "What do you think you're doing? In broad daylight — are you trying to rob someone?"

Jiyao blinked, then recognized the young man. He was a cousin of her cousin Zhao Jinde's, someone she had briefly crossed paths with at the Zhao household.

And not far behind him, her cousin Zhao Jinde was jogging over as fast as his legs would carry him.

The tight knot in Jiyao's chest unraveled the moment she spotted a familiar face.

"I am a student at the Imperial Academy," Wen the Ninth said, clearly flustered. "I am no street thug. I only wanted to speak with this young lady."

"Speak about what? Come on then, speak to me!" Zhao Jinde, all of thirteen years old, arrived in a breathless rush. Young as his face still was, he stepped in front of Jiyao with all the bearing of someone twice his size.

Now that he was close enough, Zhao Jinde realized the man blocking the road looked oddly familiar. He had seen him somewhere before.

And Wen the Ninth, in turn, had recognized his classmate's brother-in-law.

Inwardly, he cursed his luck. With this many people around, pressing the matter further was impossible. Seeing his opportunity slipping away, he had no choice but to take his leave. Even as he turned to go, he got in one last word: "I apologize for the trouble I caused, miss. I meant no offense. Everything I said was the truth."

Once he was gone, Zhao Jinde turned to his cousin. "What did he mean, 'everything was the truth'?"

Jiyao did not answer. She only shook her head. She genuinely could not understand why Wen the Ninth had felt the need to say any of that to her.

Had he not already said as much to Grandfather? And Grandfather had refused him to his face. Did he imagine she could somehow persuade Grandfather to reconsider?

Seeing that she did not reply, Zhao Jinde assumed it must have been something unpleasant, and did not press further. He quickly changed the subject, gesturing to the young man beside him. "This is my cousin Lu Ming. He came with me today to look for a book."

They had just arrived in the area when they noticed someone deliberately blocking their cousin's way. Young men's blood ran hot, and Zhao Jinde had been about to drag his cousin into the fray — only for Lu Ming to have already stepped forward before he could say a word.

"Mr. Lu, thank you for what you did just now," Jiyao said sincerely.

Lu Ming raised an eyebrow. "It was nothing worth mentioning."

He cleared his throat, about to add something modest, when he noticed that the young miss was already speaking quietly to her cousin: "Did you find your book?"

"Not yet. I'll have my cousin help me look for it after." Zhao Jinde turned back to his cousin and asked where she had been headed today.

Jiyao explained briefly, then urged him to go about his own business.

Zhao Jinde frowned with concern. "There's no rush. Let me see you two back first."

"The carriage is right there, there is no need. Go attend to what matters." Jiyao quickly insisted.

Zhao Jinde thought it over and finally relented. He walked them to the carriage, though, and saw them seated before letting them go.

The roads within the capital were smooth and well-kept, and the carriage moved quickly and steadily.

Reflecting on the strange afternoon, Jiyao felt a bone-deep weariness she couldn't quite explain.

Beside her, Shuangxi opened her mouth, thought better of it, and closed it again. Several times. At last she ventured, hesitantly: "Miss... what do you think of Mr. Lu?"

"What?" Jiyao blinked, then answered slowly, "He seems nice enough."

Not many words to him. But principled.

Shuangxi wanted to probe a little further, but couldn't quite bring herself to. Instead she murmured, half to herself: "I wonder if he's already promised to someone..."

Of all the people in Haitang Court, she worried most about the second miss's marriage prospects.

She hadn't said it outright, so Jiyao simply pretended not to catch the meaning. As for whether Mr. Lu was promised to someone or not, she gave it not a single thought.

For one thing, her marriage was entirely in Grandfather's hands. For another, she was, at present, quite satisfied with her dreams.

Everything else could wait.

...

These past few days had been consumed by preparations for the birthday gift, and Jiyao had been nearly running herself ragged. Now that things were more or less in order, she was in the mood to let herself wander freely in her dreams for once.

That evening, Jiyao lowered the bed curtains early.

Before long, she drifted into sleep.

In the dream, she was resting in her room, and someone seemed to be lying beside her.

She turned her head — and the young lord's eyes snapped open.

Jiyao smiled at him.

But he rose swiftly, lifted the bed curtain, and walked straight out without a word.

Jiyao let out a soft, puzzled sound.

Was this really what she had wanted, somewhere deep inside her — for him to leave?

Surely not. At the very least, he ought to have kissed her first.

chapters.title: Probing
chapters.content:
The second time Qin Yuan found himself sinking into that strange dream, he was not particularly surprised.

He tested his awareness and found he could move freely. Without hesitation, he rose and walked toward the door.

But he had barely taken a few steps when he suddenly lost control of the dream. Against his will, he turned back, strode to the bedside, bent down, and pressed a gentle kiss to the woman's forehead.

Jiyao tilted her face up and kissed his cheek in return, then rested her forehead against his.

Skin to skin, breath mingling, the two of them were impossibly close.

By all appearances, it was a tender and beautiful scene. But within Qin Yuan's chest, nothing resembled the warmth it seemed to project. What surged up instead was a helpless, simmering fury.

Here we are again.

Was there truly no way out of this peach blossom maze?

In the past few days, Qin Yuan had summoned an imperial physician to examine him. His body was in perfect health. Clearly, whatever was happening in these dreams had caused him no physical harm.

He could simply treat them as a spring dream and be done with it.

But he was not ready to accept that.

A man accustomed to controlling everything does not take kindly to dreams where he is wide awake and yet utterly powerless.

He needed desperately to change this.

Jiyao, for her part, had no idea what was going through his mind.

But as their foreheads rested together, a thought drifted vaguely through hers: just now, the moment he had opened his eyes, he had rushed toward the door. That was entirely unexpected. If she hadn't been consciously directing the dream, what had he actually intended to do?

The thought surfaced without warning, but once it appeared, it clung to her and would not let go.

Come to think of it, he had been a little strange in the last dream too.

The young lord was not like her parents. He was someone she had conjured from her own imagination. And that made her curious: what was it, really, that she wanted deep down?

Jiyao propped herself up on one arm and slowly sat upright.

As she moved, her dark hair cascaded around her shoulders like a fall of ink, lending her a soft and flowing beauty.

She tilted her head to one side and asked, with genuine curiosity: "Where were you rushing off to just now?"

The moment the words left her lips, she simply waited, watching him with full attention, expecting an answer.

Qin Yuan was caught off guard.

He had expected to do what he had always done in this dream, open his mouth and have insincere, pleasing words come out unbidden. But strangely, he found he was not speaking at all.

So, he had regained control of the dream?

"To the study," he said, offering an offhand reply once he understood the situation. He was certainly not going to tell her he had been trying to escape this peach blossom trap.

He would try again what had failed last time.

Jiyao let out a soft laugh, her eyes curving into crescent moons. "Are you sitting for the imperial examinations?"

She was all smiles and good humor, and had done nothing untoward. Qin Yuan suppressed his tangled emotions for now and simply answered: "No."

His features were cool, his expression unsmiling. Jiyao was not the least bit put out. She only smiled quietly to herself.

The Fang family placed great value on scholarship. A man who leaped out of bed at dawn to go to his study, so industrious, so devoted to learning, was precisely the sort her heart had always envisioned.

Without the slightest suspicion, Jiyao said with a little pout: "Then I want to come too."

Qin Yuan's gaze sharpened slightly. His eyes lingered on the pale, slender column of her throat. He said nothing.

"You read your books. I won't disturb you, truly." Jiyao said this with perfect sincerity.

Qin Yuan dropped his gaze and, still without a word, simply walked out.

Jiyao blinked, a little puzzled. But she did not stop him, and made no effort to steer the dream. She let him go of his own accord.

She was curious. If she did not direct things, what would this dream-version of him do on his own?

This time, Qin Yuan moved without obstruction.

But no matter which direction he walked, he found himself confined to the same small area: the bedchamber, the courtyard, the peach grove, the side hall. He could not get beyond them.

From this, Qin Yuan formed a theory: without the woman to lead him, he could not leave this place. Or rather, everything in this strange dream revolved around her.

Who was she?

He didn't know her name. And her face, he could never seem to hold onto.

Why was it that around her, even his ability to control a dream collapsed? He had already mastered that skill in every other dream he'd had.

"Didn't you want to go to the study?" Her voice rose suddenly at his back.

He turned. Sure enough, there she was.

Jiyao gave a quiet sigh. "Do you not know where it is? I'll take you."

Haitang Court had only one study, the room where her father had read during his lifetime. She seldom entered it herself and was even less inclined to let others set foot inside.

Even in a dream, she felt the same.

So Jiyao concentrated, and in the span of a breath, a study materialized out of nothing in the middle of the peach grove.

She had modeled it after the studies of her father and grandfather, and after the bookshop she had visited that afternoon. It was broad and bright, lined with shelves upon shelves of books. Several mounted landscape paintings even hung along the walls.

"There," she said. "That's it."

Qin Yuan said nothing. He gave her one long, penetrating look, then pushed open the door and stepped inside.

The study was full of strange things, and by now Qin Yuan was no longer particularly startled by any of them, including the one that had appeared from thin air. He swept his gaze across the bookshelves. Nothing unusual, just the usual classical texts.

Then, out of the corner of his eye, the paintings on the wall caught his attention, and an idea came to him.

Since he could never retain her face once he stopped looking at her, could he stare at her, feature by feature, and paint her likeness while he had her in front of him?

If he could preserve a portrait and draw it again after waking, then with his resources and influence, it would only be a matter of time before he tracked down her identity.

Once he found her, dealing with her would be considerably easier.

With this in mind, he spoke: "I want to paint your portrait."

"For me?" Jiyao's eyes went round with surprise. She thought: had she been spending these past few days painting a gift for Grandfather, and so somewhere inside her, hoped someone would paint one for her in return?

That made perfect sense. It made a great deal of sense.

"Yes."

Jiyao smiled and nodded. "All right. What would you like to paint?"

"You."

Jiyao paused for a moment, then her smile broke wider. "All right, all right. You paint, I'll grind the ink."

She was thoroughly delighted. To make grinding the ink easier, she rolled her sleeves up high, revealing a stretch of pale wrist and, resting against it, a twisted silver bangle that swayed as she moved.

Qin Yuan's gaze flickered. He looked away.

Jiyao cleaned the surface of the inkstone carefully, added a small amount of water to the well, then took up the ink stick and began to grind.

Meanwhile, Qin Yuan spread out a sheet of paper.

Watching him prepare, Jiyao grew a little impatient and lost the will to grind slowly. She thought it, and the inkstone was suddenly filled with just enough ink.

"There, use this for now."

Qin Yuan did not stop to question the oddity of it. He picked up the brush, dipped it, and bent his head to begin.

He had grown accustomed in recent years to absolute authority, to having every word obeyed without question. He had almost forgotten that he had once been a man of extraordinary patience, capable of bending himself as the situation required.

He called upon that patience now, focusing entirely on the portrait.

The body was easy enough, a few strokes were sufficient to suggest the slender figure of a young woman. But the face was another matter.

Qin Yuan was no skilled painter, and this was made worse by what felt like a hex: he could not retain her features in his mind no matter how hard he tried.

At first he would look, then paint. But this approach failed almost immediately.

He remembered perfectly well that her brows were gently curved, like distant hills on the horizon. And yet the moment he lifted his brush, he could not recall precisely where the arch of those brows peaked. In the end, he had no choice but to paint while looking directly at her face.

But she was standing right beside him. She was very close. The faint fragrance that clung to her gradually overpowered the smell of the pine-soot ink, and her silver bangle caught the light with every small movement, swaying back and forth.

It was distracting. More than distracting.

The restlessness coiling in Qin Yuan's chest grew sharper by the moment.

Jiyao, too, was finding it hard to stay focused. She had always heard people speak of a woman grinding ink by candlelight for a scholar as something elegant and refined. She had rather looked forward to it. But now that she was actually doing it, she found it... not particularly interesting.

Quite tedious, if she was honest.

"Sit across from me," the young lord said suddenly.

"Hmm?" Jiyao blinked. "Across from you? Oh. All right."

She assumed it must be for the painting's sake, that sitting opposite would make it easier. She had been thoughtless to stand at his side.

Jiyao carried a small embroidered stool over and settled herself on the other side of the writing desk, chin resting in both hands, watching him paint with full attention.

As for the ink, she didn't actually need to grind it by hand. She only had to think it, and the inkstone would fill itself.

She did notice, however, that his brushwork was not especially accomplished. And he was very slow.

Was painting her likeness really so difficult?

He had been at it for quite a while and had barely finished the eyebrows.

Oh. He was moving on to the eyes now.

Qin Yuan wasn't even looking down. His gaze was fixed directly on her, while his brush continued to move.

This alarmed Jiyao considerably. If he painted without looking at the paper, he might make a mess of it entirely and turn her into something monstrous. She leaned forward hastily, craning her neck to see.

The moment she bent her head, Qin Yuan lost his reference point and instantly forgot the precise shape of her eyes. His heart sank. Without thinking, he reached out with his left hand, cupped her chin, and lifted her face back up.

The grip of a warm hand, firm and sudden at her jaw, set off a faint, ticklish sensation. And at once, a rather wicked idea began to take shape in Jiyao's mind.

She remembered the second page of that little book. It had been a man and a woman, together in a study. Perhaps this was her chance to try something from it.

She had been working hard lately, after all. Coming to the dream to let herself go a little was the whole point. She had kept him company through this ink-grinding business long enough. It was time to try something else.

What had that page said? She was fairly sure there had been small notes written beside the illustration.

Jiyao thought it over, then tilted her head to one side, very slightly, letting her cheek brush against the back of his hand. Like a cat.

Qin Yuan went still.

And then, in the space of a single thought, Jiyao's shoes and stockings were simply gone. She remained perched on the embroidered stool, but her bare right foot, pale and tentative, reached slowly under the writing desk and found his leg.

Qin Yuan's expression froze.

chapters.title: The Study
chapters.content:
"My lord..." Jiyao's voice was soft as water, warm enough to wring out, her cheeks flushed a deep rose, her eyes bright and luminous.

Qin Yuan's expression, by contrast, had gone very dark indeed.

He shifted instinctively to pull away. Jiyao was not bothered in the least. She simply reached up and laid a gentle hand against his face, the sleeve of her robe trailing a faint, sweet fragrance.

He had endured a great deal in this dream already, holding himself back while he had some measure of control, all for the sake of capturing her likeness. And now that careful patience had been derailed by this clumsy attempt at seduction.

What remained of his composure was rapidly running out. His left hand dropped suddenly, closed around the woman's slender neck, and began to apply pressure.

But in almost the same instant, Qin Yuan realized he had lost control of the dream again.

Jiyao's neck was sensitive. Even the lightest touch there made her flinch. Even in a dream, some instinct rose up to resist it, pulling the reins without her even meaning to.

"Don't touch my neck." Jiyao said with a small, disgruntled pout. "I've told you that before. Have you forgotten?"

The grip in Qin Yuan's hand dissolved, not by his own choice. He was beginning to grasp what seemed to be the second rule of this dream: he could not, under any circumstances, harm her within it.

Jiyao felt she might have spoken a little sharply. She leaned in with a smile and pressed a conciliatory kiss to the tip of his nose, then said, quite generously: "You can kiss me there, though."

Once his hand had left her neck, Jiyao released her hold on the dream's direction entirely. She was in the mood for something unexpected, something she hadn't planned herself.

But the young lord did not move.

Whether she brushed her foot against his leg, or offered the clearest possible suggestion with her words, he did not respond the way any of the illustrations in that book had described. He did not pull her close, or kiss her, or settle her onto his lap.

Jiyao was not pleased.

What was this?

Did she actually want him to be a block of wood deep down?

Surely not.

Or perhaps she wanted to watch him slowly unravel under her teasing, inch by inch?

That thought rekindled her interest somewhat. She simply leaned against him and perched sideways on the edge of the desk. Then, taking her cues from the little book, she breathed softly against his ear, and, in a moment of mischief, gave his earlobe a light little nip.

The warm breath against his ear sent a sound roaring through Qin Yuan's head. His whole body shuddered once, and every drop of blood seemed to rush to a single point. On pure reflex, he shoved her away.

In the fraction of a second that followed, he realized with a jolt that he had regained control of the dream.

It lasted only a moment.

He had pushed her with more force than he intended. Jiyao had been perched precariously on the edge of the desk, completely unprepared, and she came very close to being knocked flat on top of it.

She was annoyed. This was not right at all. She had been so forthcoming, so willing. He was supposed to hold her close and kiss her, supposed to be pleased, even a little overwhelmed. That was how the second page of the book had gone.

Fine. She was done trying to let things unfold on their own. She would just have it be the way she wanted.

The moment that decision formed in Jiyao's mind, Qin Yuan felt control slip out of his hands again.
