What had come over him? To be thrown off balance by something so artless as that?

chapters.title: Unwilling to Accept It
chapters.content:
Jiyao, for her part, was entirely unaware of any of this.

In the dream, all five senses were fully alive. The cherry's sweet-tart juice spread through her mouth with great pleasantness. It was exactly the flavor she liked.

She smiled and said sweetly: "I want more. Feed me, my lord."

Qin Yuan, compelled by forces entirely beyond his control, suppressed everything churning inside him and picked out another cherry to offer her.

But Jiyao did not take it straight away. She held it in her mouth for a moment, and then, as he bent slightly toward her, she reached up, looped her arms around his neck, and with lips and tongue transferred the cherry into his mouth.

Qin Yuan had no time to react before he felt her body press against him, still wet from the pool, soaking through the light fabric of his white robe in an instant.

The thin cloth, now drenched and clinging, made every sensation startlingly immediate.

His mind gave a resounding lurch, and all the blood in his body seemed to rush toward a single point.

He moved to push her away, but her skin was slippery from the water and he could find nowhere to properly take hold.

In that moment of hesitation, Jiyao slipped free with a laugh and glided away through the water.

The cherry in his mouth had burst at some point, filling it with tartness and sweetness both. His body, meanwhile, was tight with a very different kind of discomfort.

Qin Yuan looked away and drew a slow, deliberate breath.

He gritted his teeth inwardly. A bathing scene, was it? She had gone to considerable lengths.

Since he had no control over himself in this dream anyway, capitulation was inevitable. She would get what she wanted in the end. What was the point of all this maneuvering?

But unexpectedly, the woman seemed to forget entirely what she had been building toward. She went on swimming by herself, as untroubled as a fish, drifting freely around the pool.

The dream ended without anything further happening.

Qin Yuan woke with an expression of extreme displeasure, got up immediately, and went directly to the washing room.

He was in there for a considerable length of time before he emerged again and gave a flat, measured order: "Bring water."

"Yes, Your Majesty."

He paused, then added one word: "Cold."

It was the fifth month now. Lowering himself into cold water, Qin Yuan felt himself return to himself almost at once. The heat in his blood, the anger coiling in his chest, both ebbed considerably.

But when he thought over the events of the dream, he slapped the surface of the water with force. The spray flew outward in a wide arc.

The young emperor sat there, furious and simmering and thoroughly unsatisfied.

One day, if that woman ever appeared before him in the waking world, he would make her pay for every last bit of this, whether she turned out to be a person or a spirit or a ghost or something else entirely.

He would not let a single drop of it go unanswered.

...

Jiyao had originally intended to try the fifth page of the illustrated book in this dream. But the bathing pool had appeared unexpectedly, and she had changed her mind on the spot, deciding simply to enjoy the water.

It had been a wonderfully novel experience.

She slept soundly through the rest of the night.

The next day at the academy, Fourth Sister Pinyao asked her: "Did you go to Muxiuan Courtyard yesterday, Second Sister?"

Pinyao and Qianyao, the twin sisters, were both daughters of the fourth branch. The question caught Jiyao slightly off guard.

She kept her expression calm and shook her head with an air of straightforward honesty. "I was going to. I even brought some sweets. But partway there, I felt that sweets alone were too simple a gift, and I turned back. I thought I'd wait and prepare something more proper before paying Fourth Aunt a visit."

"Oh, that explains it." Pinyao nodded. "I thought I'd heard a servant say they thought they'd seen you go that way, but then there was no sign of you. I was wondering if something had happened."

Jiyao smiled with a trace of embarrassment. "Nothing happened at all."

Pinyao tilted her head curiously. "What were you going to visit Fourth Aunt's courtyard for in the first place, Second Sister?"

"I've been working on my painting and wanted to ask Fourth Aunt's advice." Jiyao said this with full sincerity, because it happened to be true.

"Ah, I see." Pinyao let it rest.

Jiyao exhaled quietly.

Sixth Sister Mengyao, who had been listening, piped up with interest: "What painting? Let me see it."

"I'll show you later," Jiyao said, deflecting easily, and moved the conversation on.

That afternoon, not long after Jiyao had returned to Haitang Court, a maid from the fourth branch came to find her: Fourth Mistress was requesting her presence.

Jiyao's heart gave an anxious little lurch. Could this be about yesterday? Did Fourth Aunt suspect she had heard something she wasn't meant to?

She didn't particularly want to go, but refusing wasn't an option. She thought for a moment, then tucked one of her paintings under her arm before heading out.

All the way there, she quietly resolved her strategy: no matter what happened, she would simply play innocent. She would say she hadn't come inside, hadn't heard anything, knew nothing whatsoever.

Given how genuinely unassuming she was by reputation, no one ought to have any reason to doubt her.

With that decided, Jiyao felt considerably steadier.

What she had not expected was that Fourth Aunt, when Jiyao arrived in Muxiuan Courtyard, made no mention of yesterday at all. Instead, she was all warmth and softness: "What is this, child? Being formal with your Fourth Aunt? You think you can't come without bringing a gift?"

Jiyao shook her head, looking slightly flustered. "I didn't mean that. I just, I didn't want to impose on Fourth Aunt."

"Impose? Don't say such things. In my eyes, you're no different from Pinyao or Qianyao. If there's anything you don't understand, or any trouble on your mind, you can come to me any time."

Jiyao murmured a polite agreement.

Fourth Aunt then redirected easily: "So, you were going to show me some painting of yours?"

Jiyao brought out the painting she had brought along and offered it with respectful hands.

Mistress Chen Wenjun received it with a smile, studied it for a moment, then began: first a few words of genuine praise, followed by several carefully worded but clearly reasoned observations on its weaknesses.

As she spoke, she picked up a brush, dipped it in ink, and made a few adjustments to the painting directly.

She was skilled, and it was no idle claim. Under those light, confident strokes, the painting that had been slightly stiff and uncertain came alive.

Jiyao's technique was still developing, but her eye was reliable. She felt a spark of genuine delight. "That's wonderful! No wonder Grandfather said..."

She stopped herself mid-sentence.

"Hmm? What did your grandfather say?"

"He said Fourth Aunt was gifted in painting, and suggested I come to you for guidance when I could." Jiyao answered carefully.

In her heart, she genuinely hoped things could be easy: pleasant for everyone, and perhaps a little of Fourth Aunt's lingering resentment toward Grandfather might ease in time. Family harmony, after all, was better for everyone.

Mistress Chen smiled, in a way that didn't reveal much. "What do I know? There are people far more skilled than I am."

She left the comment there and offered a few more observations on the painting.

By the time the sky had grown dark, Mistress Chen suggested, without any fuss, that Jiyao stay for the evening meal.

Jiyao had no graceful way to decline and accepted. She joined the fourth branch household for dinner: Fourth Uncle, Fourth Aunt, and their four children, Pinyao and Qianyao the eldest, and below them two young boys, one of six and one of four, both at the age where a child is all energy and mischief.

With their wet nurses watching over them, the two small boys sat through the meal without making a sound, remarkably well-behaved.

The rest of the table was equally quiet. The only sounds were the occasional soft clink of dishes.

Jiyao found herself inexplicably tense throughout the meal and ate very little before setting down her chopsticks.

She did not want to overstay. She sat for only a short while after the meal before excusing herself and taking her leave.

The hour was late. Mistress Chen sent the wet nurses to put the two small boys to bed and went back to her own room to rest.

Fourth Master Fang Jing was half-reclined on the bed, watching his wife remove her hairpins, making idle conversation: "You were quite warm toward Jiyao this evening."

Mistress Chen said nothing, as though she had not heard.

Fang Jing felt the awkwardness of that and cleared his throat, picking up a book at random and flipping through the pages with a rustling sound.

Mistress Chen carefully lifted her earring free and put it into the jewelry case. Then she turned and asked: "What do you think of her?"

"Hmm? Who? Jiyao?" Fang Jing set down the book and thought for a moment, picturing his niece. "Well-behaved. Quiet. Looks like her mother. Hard to say who she takes after in temperament."

He smiled and leaned over, draping an arm around his wife's shoulder.

Mistress Chen pushed him off, her expression straightforward. "I'm talking about something serious."

Fang Jing made some vague, hopeful noise.

Mistress Chen reached for a hairpin and struck the back of his hand with it, not hard but not gently either. "I'm asking what you think about suggesting her as a match for Qingyun."

"Who? Your nephew?" The Fourth Master's smile faded slowly. He frowned. "That doesn't seem right."

"Why not? What's wrong with it?"

"Qingyun is a bit old," Fang Jing said, somewhat at random.

"A bit old? Qingyun is twenty-one. Jiyao is sixteen. Five years' difference. Not six. That's perfectly fine." Mistress Chen said. "I went back to my family's home today, and my brother brought it up again. He wants the two families to be connected by marriage. Pinyao and Qianyao are still too young, and their birth signs clash with his. I think Jiyao would be a very good fit..."

Fang Jing hesitated, then said, with some reluctance: "Let it go. My second brother passed third in the imperial examinations at nineteen. Qingyun is twenty-one and still hasn't passed the county level. That's not going to fly. Father will never agree to it."

Mistress Chen was displeased, but she knew her husband was telling the truth. If only Qingyun had been allowed to study at the Fang academy in the first place, he might have passed the county examinations by now.

She kept her irritation to herself and said, after a moment: "It's not entirely your father's decision alone."

"What do you mean?"

Mistress Chen didn't answer. She thought to herself: what if Jiyao was willing?

chapters.title: Thrill
chapters.content:
Jiyao returned to Haitang Courtyard at the hour of Xu.

It was already late. She did not look over the chess manual again, and after washing up quickly, she went to bed.

The room was perfectly still.

Before long, Jiyao drifted into a dream once more.

This time, the season in the dream had finally changed.

It was the height of summer. Cicadas cried ceaselessly outside, adding a restless edge to the heat. Jiyao lay on the bed in a light gauze robe, seeking some coolness. She turned her head and found her husband lying beside her, eyes half-closed, seemingly asleep.

Dark brows, full and defined. A straight, high-bridged nose.

The longer she looked, the more satisfied she felt. Truly worthy of being a man conjured from her own imagination -- he was beautiful even with his eyes shut.

On a whim, she quietly leaned over and pressed a kiss to his lips, thinking: the moment I kiss him, he will wake up and open his eyes to look at me.

And just as she thought it, the man's lashes fluttered, and his eyes opened.

...

Qin Yuan entered the dream to find a pair of eyes already fixed on him -- bright as autumn waters, shimmering and rippling, gazing at him with a warm, contented smile.

Their eyes met. He froze for a brief instant, then recognized her: that woman again.

She rested her cheek on one hand, half-leaning against his side. With every breath she took, a faint, delicate fragrance drifted to his nose.

The scene from the last dream suddenly surfaced in his mind. Without thinking, Qin Yuan shut his eyes again.

"Hmm?" Jiyao looked a little surprised. She kissed his lips again, then playfully nipped at the tip of his nose. "Wake up, wake up -- don't go back to sleep. Come and keep me company."

Her teasing was hardly sophisticated, but his body in this dream seemed to have its own memory.

Such a simple thing, and yet Qin Yuan already felt himself responding. He tried to hold his breath, but his throat moved of its own accord.

Jiyao's eyes brightened. She leaned in close and murmured softly in his ear, "Husband, shall we try the style on the fifth page? I wanted to try it last night, but I got too caught up in the water play and forgot."

Qin Yuan said nothing. He laughed inwardly, cold and sharp: as he knew it would be. In the end, it always came back to that.

She refused him once, and now she wanted it again.

Did she truly think she could use him as some kind of tool to be summoned and dismissed at will?

Jiyao had no idea what was going through his mind. She spoke as though she were consulting him, but in her heart, she was certain it would happen. And even if it did not, she could always steer it that way.

This was her dream, after all.

Still, Jiyao was in good spirits today, and she had plenty of time. Rather than deliberately bending the dream to her will, she simply pressed soft kisses to his lips, then to the line of his jaw.

Curiosity got the better of her, and she tentatively kissed the bob of his throat as it shifted.

Summer robes were thin, and they were lying close. Before long, Jiyao noticed something had changed in him.

She blinked, a little startled. So he is not made of wood after all, she thought.

But she was puzzled: if that was so, why wasn't he taking the next step? Could it be he didn't know what the fifth page showed?

The thought had barely crossed her mind when an image from the fifth page of the erotic manual materialized clearly in the air before them.

Jiyao thought: now surely this will work. He'll follow what's shown in the picture.

Qin Yuan's expression shifted.

And in the next instant, he found he had completely lost control of himself.

He was inwardly furious, and yet some part of him felt as though he had long since grown accustomed to this.

Without meaning to, Qin Yuan moved quickly. He gathered the young woman into his arms with surprising gentleness, kissing her carefully, attentively, as his hands worked with practiced ease at her robes.

Her skin was pale as snow, flushing now and then to a soft, faint pink. Her body was impossibly pliant -- soft beyond imagining, supple enough to fold all the way to her own shoulder.

There was no question that Qin Yuan resented all of this. He had lived so long in a position of absolute authority that he could not tolerate being controlled, being stripped of his freedom -- and yet he felt, undeniably, a rush of pleasure.

Yes -- pleasure. His mind refused to admit it, but the body did not lie.

It came like waves, one rolling over the last, each higher than the one before, until the tide surged and crested and swept over him entirely, nearly swallowing him whole.

Every stray thought was swept away in that instant.

In that moment, he stopped fighting the instinct of his own body. He simply let go. His hands closed around the smooth curve of her legs, and he went on.

Jiyao, hazy and drifting, sensed that something had shifted: wait, again?

She opened her mouth to speak, but her husband bent his head and sealed her lips with his.

They were twined together, mouth to mouth, limb against limb.

His strength was overwhelming.

Jiyao's body trembled without her meaning it to. Her thoughts blurred, and whatever she had meant to say slipped away from her, as did any intention of shaping the dream. She surrendered to it, as though this were simply what she had always wanted in the deepest part of herself, and let him do as he pleased.

When she woke from the dream, Jiyao lay with her eyes open, perfectly still.

Heavens.

She truly had not expected this of herself -- to lose herself so thoroughly, even in a dream.

It was outrageous. And thrilling.

Not a single mark anywhere on her body, and yet Jiyao felt as though every bone had gone soft, not a trace of strength left in her. A quiet, insistent reminder of what she had just lived through in that dream.

She lay there for a long while before finally slipping out of bed to tidy herself.

When she climbed back in, a faint, lingering ache still hummed through her.

She drew a slow breath and gave herself a firm, silent warning: she could not allow this again. She had to restrain herself. Even in dreams, she could not give in like this.

...

In the inner chambers of Zichen Palace.

Qin Yuan rose and went directly to the bathing room.

"Prepare water."

This time, he did not specify cold water. The attendant, not daring to decide on his own, prepared it at a comfortable temperature.

Qin Yuan said nothing further. He simply lowered himself into the water.

Warm water flowed over him. The young emperor sat with his eyes half-closed, utterly silent.

Perhaps because this dream had left him satisfied, some of the ferocity that usually haunted his brow had eased. There was still displeasure, but his mood was considerably calmer than before.

A thought even drifted through his mind: perhaps, since he could not control himself in these dreams, he should simply let it be for now.

It did no harm to his body, after all. And he could not change it regardless.

Had it not been rather enjoyable, just now, in the second half of that dream? If it could always be like that -- uninhibited, like the latter part of tonight -- perhaps there was no harm in having these strange dreams after all.

But almost immediately, Qin Yuan caught himself and forced the thought down hard.

Was he losing his mind? He was the Son of Heaven. The supreme ruler. How could he entertain such ideas?

Had he forgotten that he could not control himself in that dream?

No. He could not allow himself to go on like this.

At first light, Qin Yuan sent someone out of the palace to summon the Daoist priest Yunhe from the Ziyun Temple for an audience.

But half a day later, the messenger returned to report that Daoist Yunhe had gone out on some matter and was not at the temple. He would not return for another ten days.

Qin Yuan was deep in state affairs and did not say much. He simply waved the man away.

"Your Majesty, shall we send men to bring him back by force?"

"No."

Qin Yuan thought: ten days was nothing. He could wait.

...

Jiyao's life carried on as usual.

With one addition: her Fourth Aunt, Chen Wenjun, had recently taken to sending for her at Muxi Courtyard quite often, offering to guide her in her brushwork.

It was a kindness from an elder, and Jiyao could not decline. She applied herself earnestly.

She was already attending the women's academy, and in her spare time she studied chess manuals. Now painting was added to the mix, and her days became quite full. For several nights in a row, she did not attempt to shape her dreams at all.

On her day off from the academy, a maid from the Fourth Branch came early to urge her over to Muxi Courtyard again.

Jiyao went without thinking much of it.

But she had barely been seated for a moment when a guest arrived: her Fourth Aunt's nephew, come to pay his respects to his aunt.

Seeing that her aunt had company, Jiyao thought it best not to linger and moved to excuse herself -- but Fourth Aunt caught her by the hand.

"Where are you going, child? These are family. Sit. Let me introduce you. This is your Cousin Chen -- he loves chess, just like you. The two of you should have a game sometime." Then, turning to her nephew: "Qingyun, this is your Second Cousin."

Chen Qingyun bowed courteously. "Second Cousin."

Jiyao gave a small nod in greeting. Not wanting to intrude on their reunion, she quickly found an excuse to take her leave.

"Off you go, then." Fourth Aunt smiled easily and waved her on her way.

Jiyao left without delay and went straight back to Haitang Courtyard.

Shuangxi came in carrying glutinous rice dumplings and looked at her curiously. "Miss, you're back so soon? Weren't you at the Fourth Madam's learning to paint?"

"Fourth Aunt had a guest." Jiyao peeled open a dumpling and gave a vague answer.

The dumpling was rather sticky. She ate half and set it aside, turning her attention back to the chess manual.

The next day, to her mild surprise, she ran into Chen Qingyun at Muxi Courtyard again.

Jiyao found it a little odd, but she did not dwell on it and found a reason to leave before long.

That evening, Fourth Aunt Chen Wenjun came to find her at Haitang Courtyard.

Jiyao hurried to invite her in, and poured the tea herself.

Chen Wenjun accepted the cup, set it to the side, and smiled. "Send Shuangxi away. We have a private matter to discuss, just the two of us."

Jiyao glanced over at Shuangxi. The maid understood at once and stepped out.

"Jiyao." Fourth Aunt took her hand warmly. "There's no one else here, so I won't beat around the bush. What do you think of my nephew Qingyun?"

Jiyao's heart gave a small lurch. "Aunt, what do you mean? Think of him in what way?"

She wondered if this was about getting him into the Fang family's private academy -- perhaps her aunt hoped she might put in a word with her grandfather? But Jiyao's own standing was modest at best; her word might carry little weight.

chapters.title: Reaction
chapters.content:
"You're nearly seventeen," Chen Wenjun said with a smile. "It's time to start thinking about marriage. Your Third Sister is younger than you, and she's already engaged. Doesn't that stir any feelings in you at all?"

Jiyao blinked, and then it dawned on her what this was really about.

She steeled herself and gave a measured answer. "Marriage is a great matter. It is Grandfather's place to decide. I have no particular thoughts of my own."

It seemed everyone assumed she ought to be anxious now that Third Sister was engaged -- but in truth, she felt no such urgency at all.

"It is Grandfather's place to decide, yes, but you cannot simply leave it all to him. Your own heart matters too." Chen Wenjun smiled, her tone gentle. "Jiyao, you're such a beauty. Surely you'd want someone handsome to match?"

She had heard from her husband that this niece of his had a weakness for good looks. As it happened, her own nephew was quite striking.

Jiyao's cheeks flushed red. She did not know what to say.

Seeing her blush, Chen Wenjun took it as a promising sign and pressed on. "My nephew is handsome, upright in character, fond of chess just like you, and his parents are reasonable, sensible people. If you're willing, I'll have them send a matchmaker to speak to your grandfather at once."

Noticing Jiyao's hesitation, she added, "As for your grandfather -- don't worry about that. A match that keeps both sides of the family close? Once you've agreed, he won't hold out forever."

Since things had gone this far, Jiyao could no longer afford to weigh her words carefully. She spoke in a rush. "Fourth Aunt, I -- I can't. I don't agree to this."

"What?" Chen Wenjun faltered, certain she had misheard. "You don't think well of him?"

Her nephew might not yet have any titles to his name, but he was strikingly handsome -- a face like polished jade, lips red, teeth white, with an air of easy elegance. At this very moment he had dressed with particular care, looking more dashing than ever.

There was no shortage of young women who wished to marry him. It was only because the Chen family had been especially careful about his match that the matter had been delayed this long.

Jiyao had spent her whole life sheltered within the inner quarters and had barely laid eyes on a young man. How could she look at someone like this and feel nothing? How could she refuse so decisively?

That made no sense. Had she not fled in shyness every time they crossed paths?

"No, no, no --" Jiyao said carefully. "It is simply that this particular arrangement will not do."

A thought flickered through Chen Wenjun's mind. "Why not? Is there someone already in your heart?"

"No." Jiyao denied it at once.

Chen Wenjun had no wish to bully a young girl with her authority as an elder, but she could not help feeling indignant on her nephew's behalf. "Then is it his looks you find lacking?"

Jiyao shook her head again.

In her heart, though, she thought: handsome? He might well be, but he was nothing compared to her husband in the dreams. That was a man who truly suited her.

But of course, that was not the real point.

"Then what is it? His character? His family? His prospects?"

Jiyao could not find the words.

"I will ask once more -- do you truly refuse?" Chen Wenjun's patience was nearly spent.

Jiyao lowered her head. She thought for a moment, and at last could not help saying, "If Fourth Aunt believes the match is a good one, she is welcome to speak to Grandfather. In matters like this, it is still Grandfather who has the final word."

Not to have her agree first and then use that to pressure Grandfather into nodding along.

Jiyao was by nature timid and careful, and on the matter of her own lifelong happiness she was more cautious than ever. She would never bypass her grandfather and make promises in private.

She felt there was nothing wrong with what she had said -- it was perfectly reasonable, and befitting her position.

But Chen Wenjun's expression darkened. She let out a cold laugh. "Ah, I see. You are the Minister's granddaughter. Your standards are high. Our modest little family is not worthy of the honor."

She turned and walked out, her face set.

"Fourth Aunt, that is not what I meant." Jiyao rose and moved to follow, but could not catch up.

She let out a quiet sigh and turned back to her room.

"Miss, why did the Fourth Madam look so unhappy when she left?" Shuangxi came in from outside, puzzled.

Jiyao answered vaguely. "She is a little unhappy."

But she really did not feel she had said anything wrong.

She thought: if only dealing with people in the real world were as easy as it was in her dreams.

When Chen Wenjun returned to Muxi Courtyard, her face was still dark with displeasure.

Fang Jing took one look at her expression and guessed the matter had not gone well.

Sure enough, a moment later, his wife said with barely contained fury, "Didn't they say she has a weakness for good looks? And yet she still turns Qingyun down. Ridiculous!"

-- It was Fang Jing who had casually mentioned Jiyao's preference to his wife. He did not have much contact with his nieces ordinarily, but when Third Niece became engaged, he had asked his father about Jiyao's marriage prospects. His father had replied vaguely that the girl was like his Second Brother -- fussy about appearances, only willing to settle for someone handsome. He had repeated it to his wife as an idle joke afterward.

He had not expected her to actually take it seriously and use it as a strategy.

But how could it have worked? A family like theirs would never bypass their elders to arrange a match in private. His wife was usually sharp-minded, but when her own family was involved, she had a blind spot.

"Besides, if I truly thought Qingyun was a good match, I should have spoken to her grandfather first. Only after he agreed should I have come to her." Chen Wenjun almost laughed despite herself, half in exasperation.

Fang Jing could not help interjecting. "That is not an unreasonable thing for the girl to say. Marriage is a serious matter -- it requires the elders' approval. You know how timid she is."

Chen Wenjun shot her husband a look. "Speak to her grandfather? If her grandfather were easy to persuade, would I have gone to her first? This one isn't good enough, that one isn't good enough. I'd like to see what kind of man she ends up with."

Fang Jing quickly offered her a cup of tea and tried his best to soothe her.

Fourth Niece Pinyao and Fifth Niece Qianyao exchanged a glance and said nothing, their feelings complicated.

...

Jiyao knew she had likely offended Fourth Aunt.

After that day, no maid from the Fourth Branch came to summon her to Muxi Courtyard for painting lessons.

She gathered her courage and went to Muxi Courtyard herself, but was met only with: "The Fourth Madam is busy at the moment. Second Miss, please come back another time."

After that small flame of courage flickered out, Jiyao did not try again.

She returned to her life as it had been before.

In truth, it was not so bad. At least she had considerably more peace.

When a person is idle, the mind begins to wander.

One day, Jiyao felt the urge to shape her dreams again.

That night, as the summer heat began to ease, she lowered the gauze curtain around her bed to block the light from outside.

She sank into a deep sleep and, before long, drifted into a dream.

The dream began with Jiyao admiring flowers.

Soon she became aware she was dreaming. Her thoughts shifted, and the scene before her changed with them.

She was in Haitang Courtyard. The peach blossoms had fallen from every tree, and in their place hung large, sweet peaches.

She considered the scene and found it still not quite to her satisfaction. With another small thought, her husband stepped out from behind one of the peach trees.

Tall and beautiful, with a light, effortless bearing. Still exactly the way she liked him.

Jiyao's eyes lit up. She took a few quick steps forward and threw her arms around him. "Husband!"

...

It had been many days since Qin Yuan last entered that dream.

Tonight, somehow, he found himself in it again.

The blossoms had turned to peaches, but it was the same familiar place.

The moment he registered that he was dreaming, a soft body came flying into his arms.

Qin Yuan's instinct was to push her away, but the moment he raised his hands to do so, she stepped back from his embrace on her own and caught hold of his sleeve, pouting up at him. "I've missed you so much."

Her voice was soft and full of longing.

Qin Yuan paused. Without knowing quite why, he found himself thinking of that last dream -- of the way she had been at the end, exhausted, leaning against him, looking both pitiful and impossibly alluring.

Even so, he pulled his sleeve free without expression.

Jiyao did not notice. She only smiled and asked, "It's been so many days. Did you miss me?"

She imagined he would say: "Of course I did."

"Of course I did." The words left his mouth before he could stop them. Qin Yuan realized he had lost control of the dream again, and whatever small, inexplicable softness had stirred in him just a moment ago vanished at once, replaced by irritation.

There it was again -- that helpless, uncontrollable feeling.

Jiyao smiled warmly. "Shall we have a little conversation?"

"About what?"

"Just anything. I have so many things I've wanted to say to you."

Her thoughts shifted, and a chaise longue appeared in the middle of the peach grove.

She pulled him down beside her, intending to pour out all her recent worries. But when she tried to think of what to say, she found there was nothing she was particularly troubled by.

She had offended Fourth Aunt, yes, but Fourth Aunt had done nothing more than stop teaching her to paint and ignore her. There had been no deliberate cruelty.

She could speak of losing her parents so young -- but in her dreams, she had a mother and father, and she had no wish to shatter that illusion.

So instead, Jiyao simply rested her head in her husband's lap and toyed lazily with his fingers, rambling about whatever came to mind: swinging on the swing, learning to paint, a game of chess.

This and that, fragments and chatter.

Qin Yuan suddenly realized he could control the dream again.

And in the same moment, he noticed something else: her head was shifting restlessly in his lap, and he found himself, to his own irritation, responding to it.

chapters.title: Lucid
chapters.content:
Qin Yuan's expression darkened.

He was not certain whether this was some new form of deliberate provocation or not.

But there was no chance he would do anything out in the open air, under the sky, like this.

Without hesitation, he drew his fingers away from her grasp.

Suddenly finding her hands empty, Jiyao blinked but did not sit up. She simply tilted her head and looked up at him, red lips parting softly. "Husband, what are you doing?"

From where Qin Yuan sat, he had a clear view of those lips -- shaped like water chestnuts, opening and closing -- and the faint pink of her tongue just barely visible beyond them.

He did not know why, but his mind suddenly went back to that time by the hot spring, when he had fed her cherries and the tip of her tongue had grazed the pad of his finger.

Qin Yuan's body went taut. Almost against his own will, he slipped his finger between her lips.

Jiyao did not understand. She assumed he was playing with her, and bit down on his finger -- not too hard, not too gentle.

A small, sharp pain. It brought Qin Yuan back to himself in an instant, and his expression grew even darker.

What had he just done? He was in control of the dream, and he had voluntarily --

He moved to push her away, but Jiyao had already noticed the unmistakable change beneath his robes.

She half-sat up, looked for a moment, then said after a brief hesitation, "Then carry me back inside. But I'm saying it now -- none of that indulgence like last time. Once is enough."

Qin Yuan almost laughed, then found he had lost control of the dream again.

He said nothing. He bent down, lifted her into his arms, and carried her inside.

The sky, which had still been bright, suddenly turned dark.

The room, though, was warmly lit.

Jiyao was not particularly fond of the style on the sixth page of the manual. She wavered over whether to skip it, and turned to ask him: "Which one do you like?"

She wanted to hear her own heart, so she cleared her mind and let the answer come freely.

"None of them." The words were out of Qin Yuan's mouth before he realized -- and with them, he found he could control the dream again.

But he did nothing. He waited to see what would happen.

"What?" Jiyao looked genuinely surprised. Was her own inner heart telling her she should not lose herself in the hollow pleasures of a dream?

Was she truly this strict with herself?

But she had gone so many nights without shaping her dreams. She only wanted to relax today.

She did not dwell on it. She simply pointed at the manual. "That won't do. You have to pick one."

Qin Yuan pointed at random to the sixth page. "That one."

Jiyao looked at the page, then looked at him, then seemed about to say something before thinking better of it. After a long pause, she said, "All right. Fine. We'll try it."

She supposed it was her own curiosity at work -- she wasn't particularly fond of it, but she wanted to work through the pages one by one in her dreams, just to see.

If that was the case, then so be it.

Jiyao steadied herself, cupped his face in her hands, pressed a firm kiss to his lips, then moved to kiss the line of his throat.

Qin Yuan's body tensed. Instinctively, he kissed her back, while his hands moved with startling familiarity to remove her outer robe, kissing her almost everywhere before settling into the position on the sixth page -- guiding her to rest on her folded arms, bent forward.

He knelt behind her, poised and waiting.

But in that moment, Qin Yuan suddenly realized something: from the moment she had asked which style he preferred, all the way until now -- he had been in full control of the dream the entire time.

Which meant that everything he had just done -- the kissing, the undressing, positioning her like this -- he had done in complete and full awareness.

Qin Yuan's expression shifted.

Did he want to continue?

He was still hesitating when the world tilted -- and in the next instant, he found himself pressed onto his back, both hands and feet bound with silk ribbons, unable to move at all.

-- Jiyao had decided she did not actually like the sixth page style after all, and on a whim resolved to skip it. So she had taken control of the dream again.

Qin Yuan drew a sharp breath. He tried to revert to the way things had been and found he could not.

In the span of a heartbeat, he lost all control over the dream.

The last time, in the study, he had at least been able to hold her by the waist. This time he could not move an inch.

Humiliation and pleasure surged through him at once, and he could not tell which was stronger.

...

Jiyao found that she quite enjoyed this feeling of being entirely in charge. It was similar to that time in the study, and yet different. This style had less of a thrill to it than the others, but the sense of command and control from being above made up for it very nicely.

She braced her hands against his chest and leaned down to kiss his lips every now and then.

In less than a quarter of an hour, her mind went completely blank -- swept clean of every thought except one: she absolutely could not give in this time. She could not let it go on like last time.

To guard against losing herself, Jiyao forced the dream to an end while she still could.

She opened her eyes. Moonlight filtered in through the thin gauze curtain.

The moon was soft and hazy.

Jiyao let out a quiet breath. That was better -- only once. Thrilling, yes, but not excessive. Not indulgent.

...

That same night.

In the inner chambers of Zichen Palace.

When Qin Yuan jolted awake, his face was ashen, a vein visible at his temple, and a familiar urge to kill something rose sharply in his chest.

Unlike last time, there was nothing approaching satisfaction. Not only had his hands and feet been bound -- she had stopped things right when he was suspended in the worst possible state of tension.

He had been used as nothing more than a tool.

His body still ached with discomfort. Qin Yuan forced all other thoughts down and went directly to the bathing room.

He called for water. He submerged himself in cold water until some measure of calm returned.

The last time the dream had been so uninhibited, he had woken with the faint, foolish notion that perhaps things could go on like this. That thought had only flickered for a moment, but it had left a small crack of permissiveness somewhere inside him.

This dream had crushed that last trace of leniency completely. One or two moments of pleasure could not conceal the truth: he was trapped in these strange dreams, helpless to control himself, and it had to stop.

He had to put an end to this.

"Where is the Daoist Yunhe? Summon him to the palace at once." After bathing, Qin Yuan asked in a cold voice.

By his calculations, the man should have returned by now.

"Yes, Your Majesty."

...

The Daoist Yunhe had returned to Ziyun Temple the previous afternoon.

First thing in the morning, a messenger arrived from the palace.

This was his second audience with the emperor, and the Daoist was considerably calmer than the first time.

He waited in the side hall for approximately half an hour before the emperor received him. He bowed with great respect.

"Your method of controlling dreams is not working." Qin Yuan came straight to the point, his voice cold and flat.

Daoist Yunhe was taken aback. He had not expected to be summoned again over the matter of dreams.

He was still searching for the right words when the emperor added, "It works sometimes. Not others."

"Sometimes and not others?" The Daoist looked startled. "Your Majesty -- are there times when you are not aware that you are dreaming?"

"No. I know every time that I am in a dream." The emperor said each word deliberately. "But within the dream, sometimes I can control it and sometimes I cannot."

The Daoist furrowed his brow. That was strange.

In theory, someone who could control a dream once should be able to control it every time without fail. There should be no such thing as inconsistency.

He ventured to ask, "May I ask what sort of dreams Your Majesty has been having?"

The same person as before?

The emperor's expression went cold, his gaze sharp as a blade, but he did not answer the question. "Just tell me why the dream control fails."

Daoist Yunhe's brows furrowed deeper. Even interpreting dreams required knowing their content. Without the specifics, how was he expected to guess? He had some gift for divination, but he was not omniscient.

Faced with the Son of Heaven, however, he could only say carefully, "The precise cause, I cannot say for certain at this moment. But if Your Majesty simply wishes to no longer be troubled by these unusual dreams, that can be arranged simply enough."

"Oh?"

"Most people dream every night. Many simply wake and forget, and believe they have not dreamed at all. If Your Majesty dislikes these dreams, I have a method to make Your Majesty feel as though they never happened."

Qin Yuan's tone turned odd. "As though they never happened?"

"Yes. No memory whatsoever -- no different from a night of dreamless sleep."

Qin Yuan almost laughed. For an ordinary dream, forgetting it might be enough. But for these particular dreams -- pretending they had never occurred was nothing short of self-deception.

Still, he asked, "What method?"

"The Dream-Forgetting Pill."

Qin Yuan gave a soft sound of assent and had it brought forward.

The Dream-Forgetting Pill was no larger than a heat-relief pellet, white all the way through, with a faint, clean fragrance.

"Your Majesty, though it bears the name of a pill, it is in truth a medicine. One taken each night before sleep, and no dream will leave any trace behind."

This pill was prescribed for insomnia and nightmares, and it was not easy to prepare. Had this situation not arisen, the Daoist would not have produced it so readily.

Qin Yuan neither accepted nor refused. He only asked, "Is there no other way?"

"Adjusting the time, position, and breathing method used when falling asleep can also reduce dreaming." Seeing that the emperor seemed mildly interested, the Daoist perked up and began to explain in detail.

The Daoist tradition had a deep understanding of breathing techniques and had researched the arts of sleep for generations. Yunhe spoke at length, and only after quite some time did he finally take his leave.

Stepping out of the side hall, he exhaled slowly and wiped the perspiration from his brow.

Then his footsteps slowed.

A thought had just occurred to him. But just as quickly, he dismissed it with a small shake of his head. Impossible.

Shared dreaming was extraordinarily rare, and the emperor's situation did not quite fit the pattern.

chapters.title: Entering the Dream
chapters.content:
Qin Yuan did not use the Dream-Forgetting Pill.

He summoned the head physician from the Imperial Medical Office to take his regular pulse, and had others examine the pill carefully until they confirmed it was harmless -- then set it aside as a last resort.

In the days that followed, Qin Yuan took the Daoist Yunhe's advice and deliberately changed the time he fell asleep, the position in which he slept, and the rhythm of his breathing.

The method seemed to have some effect. For several nights in a row, the strange dream did not come. And each morning he woke with a clear head, feeling genuinely restored.

Jiyao was entirely unaware of any of this.

For her, those particular kinds of dreams -- the ones that ventured into the territory of the erotic -- were thrilling, but also rather demanding. She could not indulge in them every night.

Besides, it was now the height of summer, the days long and the nights short. Jiyao stayed up later than usual, and not wanting to be drowsy the next day, she kept herself from shaping her dreams at night. Only occasionally, during an afternoon rest, would she allow herself a little playtime.

One day, Jiyao was summoned again to her grandfather's study.

"Were you not learning to paint with your Fourth Aunt these past few days?" Minister Fang looked up at his granddaughter when she arrived. "Why have you stopped going?"

-- Though he was occupied with affairs of state and did not pay close attention to household matters, he had lately been keeping a closer eye on this particular granddaughter, and had quietly asked people to keep him informed.

Jiyao considered how to answer. Not wanting to tell the full truth, she gave a vague reply. "Fourth Aunt has been a little busy. My brushwork isn't very good anyway... and to be honest, I've always preferred chess to painting."

"You would dare lie to me?" Minister Fang glanced at his granddaughter, his expression calm but his tone carrying an edge. "The truth."

Her evasiveness told him clearly enough that something had happened.

There was no hiding from her grandfather's sharp gaze. Jiyao lowered her head and, with some reluctance, told him the full story of what had occurred.

Minister Fang heard her out, and immediately frowned. "What an absurd thing to do. What kind of elder behaves like that? Thinking only of her own nephew, and treating her husband's niece as an afterthought?"

Jiyao privately thought that it was natural for people to be closer to some than others. A nephew from one's own family and a niece by marriage were simply not the same.

But what she said aloud was, "Perhaps Fourth Aunt had her own reasons..."

She lived quietly in the inner quarters, with no parents to depend on. She had always been well-behaved and unobtrusive, never going out of her way to befriend people and never making enemies of them either. She certainly could not speak ill of an elder directly.

Minister Fang gave a short, dismissive sound. "Her reasons? What reasons? Does she not know what her own nephew is like?"

That Chen Qingyun had a handsome enough face, to be sure -- but the man was past twenty and had not even passed the entry-level examinations. Nothing to show in learning, nothing to show in arms. The Chen family might treasure him, but if she truly thought he was a fine match, why had she not come to him openly with a formal proposal? Was she afraid he would refuse outright?

There were boundaries of propriety between father-in-law and daughter-in-law. If his wife had still been alive, he would have asked her to speak to the woman privately. But his wife was gone, and it was not appropriate for him, as a father-in-law, to reprimand a daughter-in-law directly. He would have to ask his fourth son to warn his wife to stop meddling in Jiyao's marriage arrangements.

Then Minister Fang shifted the subject. "Did you not say once that you wanted someone good-looking? As I recall, that Chen boy was rather handsome. Why did you refuse?"

Jiyao glanced up at her grandfather and said quietly, "Looks alone are not enough. And besides, in a matter as important as marriage, it is still Grandfather's place to decide."

Minister Fang gave a short laugh. His mood eased slightly.

The girl was particular -- she had made that clear -- but she still deferred the final decision to him. That was something.

He did not press the matter further, only waved his hand. "All right. I understand. You may go."

"Yes, Granddaughter takes her leave." Jiyao curtsied and withdrew.

After she left, Minister Fang let out a long, quiet sigh. While he still held his position as Minister, there were already people who thought lightly of Jiyao's marriage prospects. Who knew what it would be like after he retired.

He had thought that since she was still young, there was no rush. He could take his time and wait until after the spring examinations, perhaps. But then there had been the insult from the Wen family, and now his own household pulling strings behind his back.

He would need to find Jiyao a husband sooner than he had planned.

Only a proper betrothal could put a stop to everyone else's schemes.

But who?

Minister Fang clasped his hands behind his back and thought carefully. Jiyao had her uncles, yes, but no father and no brothers to stand behind her. And she had that particular preference for good looks. That narrowed it considerably -- he would need to find someone of modest family background but upright character, someone not yet risen but with the talent and bearing to go far. Someone worth looking at.

Thinking on it, a few names did come to mind that might fit the requirements.

...

After leaving the study, Jiyao did not go straight back to Haitang Courtyard. She went first to the lotus pond.

The pond was full of broad, green leaves stretching in every direction. Here and there, a bud had just begun to peek out, small and pointed.

She had come a little too early. Jiyao felt a quiet pang of disappointment, and picked up two clean lotus leaves to take back with her.

She had barely walked a few steps when Fourth Cousin Pinyao and Fifth Cousin Qianyao came around the bend toward her.

Jiyao smiled. "Fourth Sister, Fifth --"

But the two of them acted as though they had not seen her at all. They exchanged a look, turned, and walked the other way.

Jiyao's smile faltered. Her cheeks went warm.

The first thought that came to her, oddly enough, was: at least it's summer. No one can tell if I'm flushing from the heat or from embarrassment.

To cover her discomfort, she raised one of the lotus leaves and fanned herself with it.

Unfortunately, lotus leaves are soft and pliable. The moment she applied any real force, it tore.

She looked at the ruined leaf in her hand and sighed.

She was not particularly close to Fourth or Fifth Cousin -- she was reserved by nature, and they had simply never had much to say to each other. But as cousins under the same roof, they had always been civil on the surface, always nodded and exchanged greetings when they met. Being ignored outright had never happened before.

Were they angry with her too, because she had refused the match with Chen Qingyun?

But they had been perfectly fine with her at the women's academy just a couple of days ago.

Jiyao could not work it out. She stood where she was, staring blankly at the torn lotus leaf.

Then a familiar voice broke through her thoughts. "Second Cousin, do you want some apricots?"

Jiyao looked up. It was her younger cousin Zhao Jinde.

The boy, thirteen years old, was walking toward her, and not far behind him came his older cousin Lu Ming, carrying a small basket woven from willow branches, filled to the brim with ripe, golden apricots.

Lu Ming caught Zhao Jinde's eye. The boy understood at once, grabbed a handful of apricots, and held them out to Jiyao.

"Cousin, try one."

Jiyao took only two and asked with mild curiosity, "Where did these come from?"

"Don't worry about that, they weren't stolen and they weren't taken by force." Even as he said it, Zhao Jinde bit into one himself -- and immediately his whole face scrunched up.

The expression was so comical that Jiyao almost laughed. It would have been unkind to, though, so she held it back with some effort.

Then Zhao Jinde pulled a face. "Tricked you. They're actually incredibly sweet."

"Are they?" Jiyao's eyes went wide. She looked down at the apricots in her hand, unsure which of his words to believe.

"They are." Lu Ming spoke up beside her, his tone casual and unhurried. "Family squabbles happen. Best not to take it to heart."

"Exactly. Even my sister gets angry at me sometimes, and we always make up." Zhao Jinde agreed.

Jiyao paused, and then understood. They were trying to comfort her.

They must have seen what had just happened with her cousins.

She had been about to explain that she was not particularly bothered -- but it felt like too much to get into. She simply said quietly, "Thank you. I know."

Zhao Jinde grinned.

Lu Ming's lips curved slightly as well.

The heat was pressing down. Jiyao said a quick goodbye to the two of them, took the apricots they had given her, and headed back to Haitang Courtyard. She washed them there with Shuangxi and they shared them between themselves.

After the apricots, she had a bowl of lotus leaf congee. Whatever small knot of unhappiness she had been carrying dissolved almost entirely, replaced by a thick, heavy drowsiness.

She washed her face and went to rest.

The bed curtains hung still and quiet. Outside, she could faintly hear the cicadas.

Lying there, Jiyao's mind drifted. She thought about her two cousins and their strange behavior, then somehow wandered to apricots, to cherries... to the husband she had not dreamed of in several nights.

Ah, right. Her husband. How had she forgotten him?

She would look for him in the dream this time.

Gradually, Jiyao sank into sleep, and before she knew it, found herself in a dream.

The summer heat followed her even into sleep.

Jiyao's thoughts stirred: come out, husband, come out -- and bring me a bowl of cherry ice cream when you do.

The very next instant, the thin gauze curtain parted, and her husband stepped in from behind it, holding the ice cream, the collar of his robe slightly open, his gaze deep and still.

chapters.title: Lip Rouge
chapters.content:
After several days without that strange dream, Qin Yuan had allowed himself to relax a little.

Who could have known that a short afternoon nap would pull him straight back into it.

He stood outside the gauze curtain, and the moment his eyes met hers, his mind let out a sharp ring. The scenes from the last dream rose instantly to the surface, and his gaze turned cold without him meaning it to.

Her again.

At the same moment, Jiyao's eyes lit up and she sprang to her feet. She looked at the ice cream in his hand and laughed. "It really is cherry ice cream!"

Exactly as she had imagined.

Jiyao had not been deliberately shaping the dream, which meant Qin Yuan could move freely for now.

Seeing the bright, undisguised anticipation in her eyes, he smiled to himself -- not warmly -- and took two deliberate steps back, picked up the small spoon, and put a spoonful of ice cream into his own mouth.

"Hm?" Jiyao's eyes went wide with surprise. Wait -- is that how this is going to go?

She had asked him to bring the ice cream out. Wasn't it supposed to be for her? Why was he the one eating it?

Qin Yuan said nothing and took another bite.

In truth he had little interest in ice cream, but here in this dream, while he still had the freedom to move, he felt a petty and deliberate satisfaction in denying her what she wanted.

Jiyao did not think too much of it. She took it as a small twist, a little bit of fun.

So she leaned in closer, pointed at the ice cream, then pointed at her own lips, and smiled up at him coaxingly. "Husband..."

She was asking him to feed her.

But Qin Yuan only glanced at her once and looked away.

Jiyao was surprised. Her eyes darted around, and then she stepped forward, rose up on her toes, and deliberately ate the small trace of ice cream left on his lips.

She had thought: at a moment like this, he would surely hold her waist with one arm and keep the ice cream steady with the other hand, afraid it would spill.

The woman came suddenly close, and Qin Yuan moved to push her away -- his hand even made contact with her shoulder. But in the blink of an eye, he lost control of the dream again.

His hand slid down and settled around her slender waist through the thin layer of her robe, while his head dipped to kiss those lips of hers, shaped like water chestnuts.

Warm and soft in his arms, Qin Yuan cursed inwardly: here we go again.

That feeling of being unable to stop himself, again.

The woman wound her arms around his neck, her soft body leaning into his. The mingled taste of cherry and cream drifted between their lips.

Qin Yuan felt a tingling crawl across his scalp.

And then Jiyao bit down lightly on his lip, snatched the ice cream right out of his hand, and stepped back with a grin.

His arms suddenly empty, Qin Yuan snapped back to himself, his expression shifting. "You --"

He had barely gotten one word out before Jiyao had already scooped up a spoonful and fed it to him with easy affection.

It was daytime -- not the right time for what was in the erotic manual -- but there were plenty of other things they could do. Hold hands. Share food. Trace each other's brows. Paint each other's lips.

All of them close. All of them warm.

Jiyao imagined that her husband would be delighted and would take the ice cream from her, and the two of them would share it spoonful by spoonful.

That thought was enough. Without meaning to, Qin Yuan took the ice cream from her hands and scooped a spoonful to feed her.

The ice cream was cool, tart and sweet with cherries -- perfect for summer. Jiyao took a bite and felt her spirits lift at once. She narrowed her eyes with pleasure, turned her head, and kissed the corner of his mouth. "You eat too."

She had once seen a husband and wife sharing a single portion like this.

"Mm." Qin Yuan never ate food that someone else had already eaten. But in this dream, it was not up to him.

The same spoon. The same ice cream. Fed one mouthful at a time, to each of them in turn, by his own hand.

Unlike the woman across from him, Qin Yuan tasted almost nothing.

As the cool sweetness entered his stomach, a thought flickered through his mind: this is nothing, really. The two of them have kissed more times than he can count, and done far more intimate things than this.

But the thought lasted only a moment before he crushed it.

What was this? Self-deception? Giving up and going along with it?

He was the Son of Heaven. How had he sunk to comforting himself like this?

Meanwhile Jiyao was already brightening with a new idea. "Husband, will you apply lip rouge for me?"

"What?"

"Lip rouge." Jiyao walked over to the dressing table and sat down, opening the jewellery case to reveal all manner of lip colors arranged inside.

Jiyao went to the women's academy every day and needed only to dress neatly -- she rarely painted her brows or lips. But every now and then the whim struck her.

So while in reality she owned very little rouge or powder, in her dreams everything was here in abundance, whatever she could want.

She looked through them carefully and picked one up, holding it out to him. "Here. You put it on for me."

After all, they were not going to indulge in the manual today. They had to do something.

Qin Yuan was the emperor. He had lived his entire life in comfort and authority, waited upon by everyone, serving no one. He laughed coldly to himself -- but he had no choice. He took it from her, bent his head, opened the small case, and with no instruction whatsoever began to apply the color to her lips as naturally as if he had done it before.

His fingertips moved gently across her lips, leaving a trace of vivid color.

Somehow, without meaning to, Qin Yuan found himself thinking of that day by the hot spring pool -- of her holding a cherry between her lips -- and was caught off guard by a moment of vague, unguarded feeling.

He pushed it away within a few breaths.

Ridiculous. To be drawn in by a beautiful face he could not even remember clearly?

Jiyao had no idea what was going through his mind. She looked at herself in the mirror and found the color quite satisfactory, then reached for the next one.

Normally she would simply think the color away and her lips would return to their natural shade. But in this dream, she wanted a reason to stay close to him a little longer.

His collar was slightly open, a small patch of skin visible at his chest. On a small, quiet impulse, Jiyao turned her head and pressed a clear lip print there.

With a faint coolness.

Qin Yuan went very still.

Jiyao looked up at him, lips slightly parted, eyes bright and shimmering. "Husband. Next one."

The word that rose unbidden in Qin Yuan's mind was: fox spirit.

...

Jiyao had discovered a new game.

Each time she tried a new lip color, she would kiss him once on the chest.

There was no real reason to do it -- but watching his lashes tremble, watching him hold himself together through sheer force of will, she found it inexplicably amusing.

And so before long, Jiyao had covered his chest in lip prints.

Vivid colors. Varying depths.

A thin sheen of sweat had appeared on Qin Yuan's brow. He kept his jaw tight and his expression in place, not allowing himself to make a single sound.

By the time she had worked through dozens of colors, he regained control of the dream in almost the same instant.

At that very moment, Jiyao had stretched out a finger and was tracing the lip prints on his chest. Without thinking, Qin Yuan caught her wrist. "What are you doing?"

"Nothing. Just touching." Jiyao looked puzzled. "Loosen your grip."

In the pause between words, her gaze drifted without thinking -- and landed on the obvious change in him. Something became clear to her.

Qin Yuan knew exactly what she was looking at. His expression darkened at once, and his irritation surged: so this was what all her teasing had been building toward.

And then Jiyao extended one finger and gave it a tentative, exploratory poke.

They had been close many times, but she had never looked carefully at him before. Through his clothes now, it was -- rather alarming, actually. More so than anything in the manual.

No wonder, before...

Qin Yuan gritted his teeth and said nothing. Not trusting her to stop, he simply decided: he turned toward her, closed his hand around her waist, and at the same time released her wrist and let his own fingers move downward.

Jiyao startled and waved her hands back and forth. "No, no -- it's still light outside."

She could try what was in the manual in the deep of night. But in the middle of a daytime nap, absolutely not.

Jiyao stopped him quickly and thought: he cannot move, he cannot move. He is lying in bed, perfectly still.

With that single thought, the world spun around Qin Yuan, and somehow he was already flat on his back. His arms and legs were not bound by anything, yet he could not move at all.

"What did you do to me?" Qin Yuan's heart went cold. The words came out of him.

It was strange -- that he could speak at all right now.

But he had no time to think about that. The urge to kill something surged up in him again.

Jiyao shook her head, smiling a little shyly. "Nothing. I just want to talk."

-- If she had not decided to linger in the dream a little longer today, she would have ended it already.

She sat beside him, looked at the lip prints on his chest, then looked at the obvious state of him, and felt that this was perhaps not quite right.

But it was daytime in the real world, and she truly did not dare do anything reckless at this hour.

After a moment's thought, she hit upon an idea. With a small shift of thought, the few robes still on him slipped away.

A sudden chill swept over him, and Qin Yuan felt a rush of heat rise sharply in response. He found himself, for the first time, genuinely regretting that he had not taken the Dream-Forgetting Pill before his nap. At least then he would not have to remember any of this when he woke up.

He was still thinking about it when a soft, slightly cool hand closed around him.

Qin Yuan's whole body locked up. He drew a sharp, silent breath and barely kept from making a sound.

Jiyao frowned. She found she could not manage with one hand, so she simply used both.

In her dreams, she had been going through the manual in order, page by page. After skipping the sixth page last time, her thinking had grown more flexible.

It did not have to go in order. Was it not better to do the most fitting thing for the moment?

For instance, right now -- he clearly wanted to, but she could not. So she could do this instead.

How was it described in the manual again?

Jiyao tilted her head and tried to remember carefully.

Qin Yuan felt as though his body were about to come apart, and yet he could not move a single inch.

At last he gritted his teeth and said in a low voice, "You -- move your hands."

"Hm? Oh. Alright." Jiyao had already recalled the relevant passage and set to work.

It was a pity, really -- this particular thing was a bit dull to do. After only a short while, she was already thinking about stopping.

But then she glanced over and saw him -- face flushed, jaw clenched, eyes hazy beneath a thin film of something that was trying very hard to be restraint and failing to hide the wanting underneath -- and without knowing why, a strange little feeling stirred in her chest.

How odd. She was usually such a quiet, well-behaved person. Why did she have this sudden urge to torment him a little?

But he was still the husband she had imagined into being, and she was not truly willing to be cruel to him. So she only watched his face with soft attention.

...

At last, Qin Yuan let out a breath and felt some relief.

Something new and strange stirred in Jiyao too.

So that really works as well? And if that works, then what about the other things further in the manual?

She looked down at her hands, and with a thought, a copper basin of clear water appeared at the bedside.

She washed her hands and dried them clean with a cloth. Then, thinking it over, she took another cloth and gently wiped the lip prints from his chest.

-- She could have made them disappear with a single thought. But she wanted to do it this way. It felt like discovering a new way to play with a favorite toy.

The cloth was slightly cool and still held a few drops of water. When it touched him, Qin Yuan's body went rigid again.

Her hair was pinned up, but one or two wayward strands had fallen loose, trailing over him, tickling unbearably. The faint, delicate scent of her went straight to his head.

Qin Yuan had barely begun to recover when that familiar, impossible feeling returned.

He closed his eyes briefly. With something of a what-does-it-matter feeling settling over him, he said in a low voice, "Sit up."

"Hm?" Jiyao blinked, and then understood what he meant.

So she did want to, deep down?

Jiyao was not particularly surprised at herself.

She hesitated -- but it was still daytime, and she held firm. She shook her head. "No, no. Tonight, we'll talk about tonight. Tonight we can..."

She could control the dream for a little while at night. That would be fine.

Qin Yuan had no sooner spoken than he regretted it, closing his eyes slightly, pressing his lips together. Had he lost his mind? He had just asked her -- of his own accord -- to sit up?

It had to be because in this dream nothing he said was ever truly his own.

And then she refused him.

Qin Yuan's expression turned darker still.

He bit down and let two words out: "Fox spirit."

Jiyao paused. She bent down, kissed him on the lips, then reached up and touched his ear, smiling. "What fox spirit? I'm nothing of the sort. I'm a person."

Such an ordinary sentence. But the moment Qin Yuan heard it, something changed in his eyes. It was as though a light flashed through his mind, and he was suddenly, sharply alert. "You're a person?"

"Yes." Jiyao nodded, perfectly serious.

In dreams, if she chose, she could fly and vanish, soar through clouds, become anything at all -- fairy, demon, ghost. But she was used to being human. She wanted to be human.

So in most of her dreams, she and her mother and father were ordinary people. Even the imagined husband before her was a person, not some demon or creature.

In an instant, image after image surfaced in Qin Yuan's mind. The words nearly burst out of him. "Are you from the capital?"

She spoke in refined, standard speech. And in one of these dreams, the place they had gone out to had felt something like the old streets of the Eastern Market in the capital -- and yet not quite the same.

Jiyao was startled. She was about to answer when she suddenly heard Shuangxi's voice calling out: "Miss! Miss!"

She jolted awake and ended the dream at once.

...

Qin Yuan woke to find himself still reclining on the daybed.

He opened his eyes and glanced at the hourglass on the table. All of that had happened in a single nap?

His body was still uncomfortable. He pushed the thought aside, rose, and went to the bathing room.

The attendant eunuch was sharp and well-practiced at reading his emperor's moods. The bath water had been prepared before Qin Yuan even emerged.

Qin Yuan took in the sight of it without a word and submerged himself entirely.

His eyes half-closed, he was still turning over the dream in his mind.

All the embarrassing parts he deliberately set aside. Only one thing kept echoing in his ears: "What fox spirit? I'm nothing of the sort. I'm a person."

He had made any number of guesses about this woman's identity. Each one had been disproven in turn.

From what the Daoist Yunhe had implied, she was neither spirit nor ghost -- and yet did not quite seem human either. As though she simply did not exist anywhere within the three realms and five elements.

And yet now she had said it herself: I am a person.

She was a person?

He still did not understand how she did what she did within his dreams -- but if she truly was a living person...

Qin Yuan's eyes narrowed slightly. Something ignited in the depths of his chest, quiet and sudden, like sparks catching.

If she truly existed somewhere in this world, then the scope of his search had narrowed considerably.

He did not yet know her face, her name, her age, or where she lived. But Qin Yuan believed, with the resources and reach available to him, that as long as she was real and she was out there, he would find her.

The thought of one day being able to drag her in front of him made his heart give a sharp knock, and his breathing came a little faster.

After bathing, he considered summoning Daoist Yunhe to the palace again. But on reflection -- the man was mediocre. He had not been able to determine the woman's origins, had not been able to explain why the dream control failed, and his only solutions were forgetting and reducing. And Qin Yuan had no wish to share the details of his dreams with anyone. He would not summon him.

He had his own way of finding her.

...

Inside the Minister's residence.

Fang Jiyao opened her eyes in a hurry, and breathed a silent sigh of relief.

Thank goodness. She had managed to restrain herself in the dream. If she had actually gone ahead with things, and then been woken up so abruptly -- there would not have been time to tidy herself.

"What is it?" She gathered herself and lifted the gauze curtain.

Shuangxi stood outside, smiling so widely she could not contain it. "Miss, the eldest young master and his family are back."

"Elder Brother is back?" Jiyao blinked.

Her eldest cousin Fang Can was the firstborn son of the main branch -- the finest of their generation. He had passed the imperial examinations at twenty-one and had been posted away to serve as an official in another part of the country for several years now. Why had he suddenly returned?

It was not the right time of year for him to come to the capital to report on his work.

"Yes -- he's been transferred back. He'll be staying in the capital from now on." Shuangxi was beaming. "He brought a great many gifts from his posting and is dividing them among the household as we speak. He also brought his little daughter -- I hear she is an absolute beauty. You should go have a look too, miss."

She knew her mistress -- not one to push herself forward, but not one to hang back either. Something like this, she would want to be present for. So Shuangxi had woken her even though she was still in the middle of her nap.

"You're right, I'll go at once." Jiyao dressed quickly and pinned up her hair. After a moment's thought, she took the longevity lock she had prepared earlier for her little niece and made her way to Shimei Hall, where the main branch resided.

When she arrived, everyone was there -- everyone except her eldest cousin himself.

She was told he had gone to the Ministry of Personnel.

Officials returning from postings away from the capital were required to report there without delay.

Her eldest cousin's family had been away from the capital for several years, and no one was more moved by their return than the main branch itself. Her eldest aunt, who had always been in poor health, stood with eyes reddened, while her younger cousin Mengyao was already curiously entertaining the little girl in their sister-in-law's arms.

The two-year-old was exactly as Shuangxi had said -- bright eyes, snow-white skin, and a pair of dimples that appeared whenever she smiled. She was lovely.

Just as she always had, Jiyao quietly found her place at the edge of the gathering.

When the little girl was brought around to greet each of her elders in turn, Jiyao offered her prepared gift and said a few polite, unremarkable words.

After a while, people began to drift away. Jiyao left Shimei Hall with the others.

She had known that her eldest cousin would be distributing gifts among the household. But seeing what had been set aside for her when she returned to Haitang Courtyard, she still stopped and stared.

"This much?"

Shuangxi answered, "Yes -- I was afraid there had been some mistake, so I quietly asked the person who delivered it. They said it was all correct, and that the eldest young master had personally specified it."

After a pause, Shuangxi added in a lower voice, "I heard he divided it by branch -- Third Branch, Fourth Branch, they all received about the same amount."

Jiyao was even more surprised. So the amount set aside for her alone was roughly equivalent to what each of the other branches received as a whole?

That was an unusual way to divide things.

Shuangxi smiled. "Never mind the how of it. The eldest young master had it sent over, so we'll just accept it."

Jiyao gave a quiet sound of agreement and said nothing more. She privately thought she ought to find some occasion soon to send something over to her eldest cousin's family in return.

Otherwise she would feel thoroughly embarrassed.

That evening, the Fang household gathered together to welcome Fang Can and his wife home.

The guests of honor were undoubtedly the eldest cousin and his wife -- the evening had little to do with Jiyao. She found a seat beside her third cousin Zhiyao, and the two of them ate their meal quietly side by side.

At some point during the banquet, Zhiyao poured her a cup of something. "Second Sister, try this. It's a new plum wine -- sweet and sour, really quite good, and it won't go to your head."

"Mm." Jiyao rarely drank, but the wine was a pretty color and carried a faint, sweet fragrance. She was tempted. She picked up the cup and took a sip.

It was tart and sweet and light on the palate. She liked it.

"Didn't I tell you?" Third Cousin grinned.

Jiyao smiled back. "You did. It really is good."

And she slowly finished the cup.

Zhiyao, seeing that she liked it, refilled it at once. "Come on, let's have another."

They each had a second cup, and even clinked their cups together quietly, mimicking the adults.

Jiyao almost never drank, and her tolerance was low. The plum wine tasted no stronger than sweet juice at first, but it had a significant delayed effect.

It had seemed perfectly fine while she was drinking it -- but by the time the banquet ended and people began to leave, Jiyao noticed her head had gone rather heavy and strange.

She could hardly believe it. Two cups, and she was already nearly drunk?

Not wanting to embarrass herself in front of everyone, she kept herself as steady as she could and took Shuangxi's arm to make her way out.

She had only gone a few steps when a voice stopped her.

"Second Sister, wait."

Jiyao paused, startled, and turned. In the lamplight beneath the eaves she recognized her eldest cousin Fang Can, who had only returned today.

He was considerably older than her, and had always had a precise, proper manner about him -- the two of them had rarely exchanged more than a few words. That he was calling to her now was genuinely unexpected.

She steadied herself and curtsied with careful respect. "Elder Brother. Was there something you wished to say?"

"You --" Fang Can's gaze settled on her. He hesitated for a moment. "Have these years been... all right for you?"

Jiyao found the question a little baffling, but nodded. "Quite all right."

Much the same as when he had left.

As she spoke, her head tilted slightly to one side, her cheeks flushed -- the effects of the wine showing themselves a little despite her efforts.

"I see." Fang Can seemed to want to say more, then thought better of it. "Good. You should go and rest."

Jiyao was puzzled but could not think why. And her head was too hazy right now to think carefully about anything.

She smiled at him and turned to go.

...

Fang Can watched his cousin's retreating figure for a long moment.

Despite the exhaustion of several days of travel, he did not go straight to his room to rest after leaving the banquet. Instead he went to the front courtyard study to see his grandfather alone.

Fang Can had grown up close to his grandparents and had always been near to his grandfather especially.

He was older now, his days full with official duties, and it had been a long time since they had spoken properly. But this visit was not for idle conversation.

"You must be tired after such a long journey. Why aren't you resting?" Minister Fang's voice was warm, though his eyes did not miss the shadows under his grandson's eyes.

Fang Can was quiet for a moment. "There is something I have been turning over in my mind, Grandfather. I felt I needed to tell you."

"What is it?"

"On the road back to the capital, I passed through Yizhou. I saw a woman there." Fang Can paused. "Her features... bore a resemblance to Second Aunt."

Minister Fang stilled. "What did you say?"

He knew this grandson's nature well -- careful, measured, never given to exaggeration. If it had been only a passing similarity, he would never have brought it up at all.

"You are certain you did not mistake her?"

"I do not believe I was mistaken. And yet the woman did not seem to recognize me. Even when I gave my name and family, her expression did not change."

That was the part Fang Can could not reconcile. If it truly was Second Aunt, why would she have gone so many years without sending word to the family -- when Jiyao was still here? And yet if it was not her, the resemblance was far too close. Even the small mole between her brows was identical.

Could two people truly look so alike?

Minister Fang's expression became grave. After his second son's death, his daughter-in-law -- née Lin -- had disappeared while traveling outside the city walls for a memorial offering. No trace of her had ever been found, living or dead.

The family had searched with everything at their disposal. For years, nothing.

"Can," Minister Fang said at last, looking at his grandson, "what is it you think?"

Fang Can shook his head. "I do not dare say for certain."

He had been old enough, when Second Aunt disappeared, to remember her face clearly. That day in Yizhou, he had caught only a brief glimpse. But in that single instant, he had been certain it was her.

And yet the woman had shown no sign of recognizing him at all.

"Did you try to learn anything about her? Who she was, where she lived?"
